findings.title: A resting limit in ZB/ZN earns a near-constant ~0.4-0.6 ticks of price improvement per fill, regardless of depth, timeframe, or shape — and that constant sits just BELOW the cost floor
findings.observation: Take every tradable 5-min bar in discovery, rest a limit N ticks from the close with a 6-bar TTL, and measure the forward close change from the fill price. In ZB the buy side pays +0.34/+0.39/+0.33/+0.19 ticks at 12 bars for depths 1/2/3/4 and the sell side pays +0.47/+0.56/+0.60/+0.62. Averaging the two sides (which cancels any directional drift in the sample) gives the pure liquidity-provision component: +0.407, +0.474, +0.466, +0.405 ticks at depths 1-4. ZN gives +0.513, +0.622, +0.636, +0.591. Resampling to 15-min (multi_scale 3) and 30-min (multi_scale 6) and repeating with depths 1-8 ticks does NOT scale this up: ZB 15-min peaks at +0.552 (depth 3, h=12), ZB 30-min at +0.763 (depth 8), ZN 15-min +0.703 (depth 4), ZN 30-min +0.811 (depth 4). Over three orders of holding time and eight depths, this quantity never leaves the band +0.30 to +0.81 ticks. It is the same number everywhere. Unconditional 12-bar drift in ZB is only -0.053 ticks and in ZN -0.023 ticks, so this is not directional drift.
findings.markets: ZB, ZN at 5/15/30-min; ES measured and found to behave differently (see negative results)
findings.robustness: Validated against a driftless tick-grid martingale built from the same bar geometry (sub-bar +-1 tick symmetric walk, per-bar sd matched, prices exactly on the tick grid so there is no rounding bias): core.touch_conditional returns d12 in [-0.080,+0.057] and edge_ratio in [0.983,1.017] across three seeds and depths 1-6, versus +0.34..+0.78 and 1.14..1.19 on real ZB. So the measurement does not manufacture this; it is a real property of the price series. Cross-market: ZB +0.474 vs ZN +0.622 at depth 2 (same sign, same order). Cross-scale: present at all three timeframes in both markets. Split-half of the full touch-conditional quantity is stable (ZB depth 6 sell: H1 +0.914, H2 +1.339; ZB depth 8 sell: H1 +1.377, H2 +1.974; ZN depth 4 sell: H1 +0.589, H2 +0.984). Session breakdown for ZB depth 6 sell d24: asia +1.063 (n=828), eu +1.330 (n=2648), us +1.083 (n=4230) — present in all three. Vol: volHI +1.276 (n=6519) vs volLO +0.461 (n=1463) — roughly 3x stronger when ATR is above its trailing-month mean.
findings.economic_why: This is payment for immediacy. The counterparty is whoever is crossing the spread to get filled inside a 5-minute bar's wick; you are standing at the extreme of the wick and being paid the pullback. It is a believable story and the martingale control confirms the 5-min bar series has genuine negative short-horizon autocorrelation that a martingale does not. But the payment is set by the same competition that sets the spread, so there is no reason to expect it to exceed a retail cost structure — and it does not.
findings.exit_evidence: MFE/MAE from fill over 48 bars, ZB depth 2 sell: mfe_p50 5, mfe_p80 14, mae_p50 5, mae_p80 13, edge_ratio 1.187 (martingale: 1.013). The excursion asymmetry is real but tiny — mean MFE exceeds mean MAE by ~15-19%, and both are 5-14 ticks, so any stop wide enough to survive p80 MAE (13-17 ticks) is far larger than the 0.5-tick edge being harvested. On the validated one-position-at-a-time simulator the best exit geometries all had a SMALL target (4-8 ticks) against a WIDE stop (12-24 ticks); every geometry with a tight stop lost. Time/market exits are strictly worse than limit-target exits because the market exit alone costs 1.0 tick.
findings.tradeable_form: Not tradeable. For the record the form would be: resting sell limit 2 ticks above the prior 5-min close, TTL 6 bars, exit limit +4 ticks / protective stop -16 ticks, forced flat at EOD. Measured net on the validated greedy simulator (one position at a time, commission 0.144t + 0.5t adverse buffer + 0.5t stop slippage + 1.0t time-exit slippage): ZB best-of-63 exit geometries +0.150 t/trade (t=0.65, n=1403), ZN best-of-63 +0.288 t/trade (t=2.15, n=3240); median across the 63 geometries -0.058 (ZB) and -0.053 (ZN). The same simulator on martingale controls returns -0.46 to -1.26, so the real market genuinely beats a random walk by ~0.6-1.0 ticks — that gap is exactly the effect above, and it is entirely consumed by the cost floor.

findings.title: In ZB and ZN, deep limit fills are asymmetric: a sell limit filled on a fast pop is followed by a give-back, a buy limit filled on a fast dip is followed by more downside. ES is the exact mirror (momentum). Real, cross-market, null-beating — and still short of cost.
findings.observation: Rest a limit D ticks away with a 6-bar TTL and measure only the PREDICTIVE part (forward close change from the fill BAR's close, which strips out the mechanical wick-pullback). ZB: buy side -0.059/-0.255/-0.342/-0.605 ticks at 24 bars for D=2/4/6/8; sell side +0.251/+0.409/+0.691/+1.159. The gap widens monotonically with depth. ZN: buy +0.004/-0.077/-0.123/-0.385, sell +0.148/+0.237/+0.331/+0.734. Measured from the limit price instead (what a fill actually earns), ZB depth 8 sell gives d24 +1.675, d48 +1.915, d96 +2.680 with edge_ratio 1.252, while ZB depth 8 buy gives d24 -0.305, d48 -0.634, edge_ratio 0.931. ES inverts completely: at an ATR-scaled depth of 3x ATR, the buy side gives d24 -0.333 and the sell side d24 -3.238 — i.e. fast ES moves CONTINUE in both directions. So bonds give back fast rallies; equities extend fast moves.
findings.markets: ZB, ZN (reversion on the sell side); ES (momentum, both sides)
findings.robustness: Misalignment null (circular whole-day shift of outcomes vs the fill bars, 300 draws) on the predictive component: ZB depth 4 z=+2.53 (h24) / +2.52 (h48); depth 6 z=+2.80 / +2.69; depth 8 z=+3.51 / +3.00. ZN depth 4 z=+2.01/+2.63; depth 6 z=+1.85/+2.18; depth 8 z=+2.93/+2.63. Cross-market: same sign and same monotone-in-depth shape in ZB and ZN — but these are two bond contracts sharing one macro regime, so treat it as roughly one independent observation, not two. Split-half of the FULL touch-conditional quantity is stable (ZB depth 8 sell H1 +1.377 / H2 +1.974). Split-half of the PREDICTIVE component alone is NOT: ZB depth 6 asymmetry (sell minus buy) is +0.072 in H1 and +1.745 in H2; ZN is -0.384 in H1 and +1.179 in H2. So the directional half of this finding lives almost entirely in the second half of discovery (roughly 2024-09 onward) and must be treated as regime-dependent. Monthly: ZB depth 8 sell positive in 14/17 months, ZB depth 6 sell 12/17, ZN depth 4 sell 15/21. Sessions all positive. volHI ~3x volLO.
findings.economic_why: Plausible: a bond futures pop of 4-5 ATR inside 30 minutes is usually a liquidity event (a data print, a block, a stop cascade) rather than a repricing, and dealers who were run over lean back into it. The mirror-image behaviour in ES — where fast moves extend — is consistent with equity index flow being more informed/trend-following. What weakens the story is that the ZB/ZN directional half only shows up in the second half of the sample, which is when the bond selloff ran; a short-biased conditional edge in a falling market is exactly the confound to be suspicious of, even though the unconditional 12-bar drift is only -0.053 ticks and cannot arithmetically account for +1.16.
findings.exit_evidence: ZB depth 8 sell fills, 48 bars from fill: MFE p50 9 / p80 22 ticks, MAE p50 8 / p80 18 ticks, edge_ratio 1.252 (best edge_ratio found anywhere in this campaign; the all-bar baseline is 1.173 and a martingale is 1.00). Exits: a 63-cell target x stop grid on the validated one-position-at-a-time simulator with honest costs put every winner at a small target (4-8 ticks) against a wide stop (12-24 ticks); the single worst geometries were large targets with tight stops (ZB -0.424 at target 16 / stop 12). Best measured: ZB depth 6, target 6, stop 16 -> +0.150 t/trade (t=0.65, n=1403, 8/17 months positive); ZN depth 4, target 4, stop 24 -> +0.283 t/trade (t=2.15, n=3240, 13/21 months positive, +$14,326 over discovery). Both are best-of-63 and neither clears a Bonferroni-style bar.
findings.tradeable_form: Closest tradeable form: ZN, resting SELL limit 4 ticks above the prior 5-min close, TTL 6 bars, on fill place a limit target 4 ticks below the fill and a protective stop 24 ticks above, max hold 96 bars, forced flat at EOD, one position at a time. Measured net +0.283 ticks/trade = +$4.42/trade, 3,240 trades in discovery. Do NOT deploy on this evidence: it is the top cell of a 63-cell exit scan at t=2.15, the directional component fails split-half, and the equivalent ZB configuration only reaches +0.150 (t=0.65). It is worth exactly one confirmatory pass on the VALIDATION split — that is a cheap, decisive test and it is the single highest-value follow-up in this report.

findings.title: The ZB/ZN limit-fill edge is 100% entry price-improvement geometry and 0% prediction — its entire size is set by one thing this data cannot measure: queue fill probability at the touch
findings.observation: Every touch-conditional outcome decomposes exactly into two terms: SNAPBACK = (close of the fill bar − limit price)×side, and POST-FILL DRIFT = (close h bars later − close of the fill bar)×side. Measured on all 70,580 tradable ZB discovery bars and 94,464 ZN bars, resting a limit 2 ticks away with TTL 6: ZB snapback +0.388/+0.431 ticks (long/short), post-fill drift at 12 bars −0.002/+0.130; ZN snapback +0.538/+0.525, post-fill drift +0.072/+0.110. The snapback term is flat in depth (ZB long: 0.357, 0.388, 0.372, 0.354, 0.281, 0.240, 0.145 at depths 1,2,3,4,6,8,10) — it is simply how far a 5-min bar closes back from its own extreme, i.e. the half-spread the market pays a passive order. Post-fill drift is ~zero and unstable (see negative results). Now the decisive part: if instead of assuming you fill whenever price merely TOUCHES your price, you require the bar to trade 1 tick THROUGH it, the snapback flips to −0.61/−0.63 and the identical trade goes from +0.47 to −0.53 ticks. Algebraically the two assumptions differ by exactly 1.000 tick of entry price, which is larger than any effect measured anywhere in this study. So the correct output is not an EV, it is a BREAK-EVEN QUEUE PROBABILITY q*: split fills into G = bars that traded through the limit (you certainly fill, EV eG) and M = bars that only kissed the limit and turned (you fill with unknown prob q, EV eM), then q* = −nG·eG/(nM·eM). Measured for the full round trip (limit in at depth 2, limit out at +2, stop 12, max hold 24, commission charged, stop slippage 0.5t, time-exit slippage 1.0t): ZB long q*=0.589, ZB short q*=0.544, ZN long q*=0.467, ZN short q*=0.475 (per-bar event view). Under the deployable one-position-at-a-time sequencing with BOTH legs subject to the same q, q* rises to ~0.30–0.35. eM (the kiss-only bars) is worth +2.43 to +2.55 ticks each; eG (the through bars) is worth −0.63 to −0.75 each. The trade is a pure bet on being filled on the bars where the market kisses your price and turns.
findings.markets: ZB and ZN (primary); ES and GC measured as controls
findings.economic_why: You are the liquidity provider. The counterparty is whoever must trade immediately at the extreme tick of a 5-minute bar — a market order, a stop being triggered, or a hedge being lifted. They pay you the spread; you accept the risk of being run over. This is a real, well-understood economic function, and the payment for it (≈0.4–0.55 ticks of price improvement, ≈$12–17 in ZB, $6–8 in ZN) is the right order of magnitude for a 1-tick-wide book. The reason it is not free money is adverse selection: on the bars where you are certainly filled (price traded straight through you), you lose 0.63–0.75 ticks. You only get paid on the bars where you are least likely to be at the front of the queue. This is the standard market-maker's dilemma and it is entirely a queue-position question, not a forecasting question. The 5-min OHLCV data cannot resolve it — there are no quotes and no book. Live fill logs from the bot itself are the ONLY way to measure q, and measuring it is worth more than any further mining of this data.
findings.exit_evidence: MFE/MAE from the fill, 12-bar window, ZB depth 2: MFE mean 2.6–4.7 ticks and MAE mean 1.4–7.5 ticks depending on hour, edge_ratio 0.95–2.38. Exit grid measured directly (ZN depth 2, touch-fill): target 2 / stop 24 net +0.471, target 2 / stop 12 +0.466, target 2 / stop 6 +0.422, target 3 / stop 12 +0.421, target 4 net lower. So target = 2 ticks is the optimum and it is flat between stop 12 and stop 24 — take stop 12 because it frees the margin slot sooner. Outcome mix at target2/stop12/maxhold24: p(target)=0.87, p(stop)=0.05, p(time)=0.08, mean hold 5.0 bars (25 min). Wider targets simply hold the slot longer for the same money: $/slot-hour falls from $17.4 at target 2 to $8.9 at target 3. Deeper entries raise $/slot-hour in ZB (depth 4 = $28.1/h vs depth 2 = $25.3/h) but raise q* from 0.544 to 0.589, so depth 4 is only correct if slot scarcity binds hard.
findings.robustness: Depth curve is a PLATEAU, not a spike: q* at TTL 6 across depths 1,2,3,4,6,8 = ZB long 0.608/0.589/0.641/0.756/1.120/1.374; ZB short 0.631/0.544/0.581/0.589/0.841/1.026; ZN long 0.507/0.467/0.523/0.655/1.043/1.389; ZN short 0.526/0.475/0.527/0.617/0.915/1.167. Minimum at depth 2 in all four cells, with depths 1–3 within 0.06 of the minimum, then monotone deterioration — a genuinely robust plateau. TTL is monotone: q* rises with TTL in every cell (ZN long depth 2: 0.430/0.446/0.467/0.498 at TTL 2/3/6/12), so short TTL is more robust per fill. Deployable sequential sim (one position at a time, one side per slot, 11:30–14:30 UTC excluded, both legs at fill prob q), net ticks per trade [disc_h1 / disc_h2 / validation], n = 1,343–4,120 non-overlapping trades per cell: at q=0.5 ZB short +0.312/+0.234/+0.394 (z 4.57/2.96/4.38), ZB long +0.377/+0.046/+0.607, ZN short +0.408/+0.329/+0.546 (z 6.69/4.41/7.88), ZN long +0.311/+0.211/+0.706. Positive in 12/12 cells at q=0.5; at q=0.3 it is 6 positive, 5 near zero, 1 negative (ZB long disc_h2 −0.303). Weakest cell everywhere is ZB long in disc_h2. Validation (Jun–Dec 2025) is consistently BETTER than discovery, so there is no decay. Cross-market agreement is close to exact. Misalignment null (day-shifted outcomes) run on the post-fill directional term only: ZB short z=2.30, ZN short z=3.02, ZB long z=−0.61, ZN long z=1.04 — the directional term is real in the short leg but only +0.126/+0.132 ticks, 6x below the cost floor, so it is not what pays.
findings.tradeable_form: Per margin slot, ONE side only (do not quote both sides from one slot — measured: quoting both sides from a single slot cut ZB net from +0.35 to +0.09 ticks at q=0.3, because whichever side fills is always the adversely-selected leg). Run up to 4 slots: ZB-bid, ZB-offer, ZN-bid, ZN-offer. While flat, each bar re-price a resting limit 2 ticks from the last close (3 ticks acceptable in ZB; never 4+). TTL 3 bars (15 min) — TTL 2 has the lowest q* but halves fill count; TTL 12 is measurably worse. On fill: resting limit exit at +2 ticks, protective stop at −12 ticks, hard flatten at 24 bars (2 h). Do not quote between 11:30 and 14:30 UTC. Expected 10–15 fills per slot per day, mean hold 5–6 bars, $13–30 per margin-slot-hour in ZB and $7–19 in ZN if q≈0.5. DEPLOY THIS AS AN INSTRUMENTED MEASUREMENT FIRST: log, for every resting order, whether the bar's extreme reached the order price and whether it filled. Thirty days of that gives q directly, and q is the entire trade.

findings.title: 11:30–14:30 UTC is a toxic fill window in both ZB and ZN — fills there are immediately run over, and it is the single largest controllable loss in the book
findings.observation: Splitting every fill (depth 2, TTL 6) by 30-minute UTC bucket, fill quality collapses in a tight, repeatable window. Mechanical price improvement (snapback) drops from a typical 0.44–0.55 ticks to 0.048 at 13:30 UTC and 0.108 at 12:30 UTC in ZB longs, and to 0.262 at 12:30 in ZN shorts. Mean adverse excursion in the 12 bars after the fill explodes from 1.4–3.5 ticks (00:00–11:00 UTC) to 6.1–8.5 ticks (12:00–14:00 UTC). The probability of being 4+ ticks underwater within an hour of the fill (P(MAE12 ≥ 4t)) goes from 0.08–0.21 in the Asian hours to 0.55–0.64 at 12:00–13:30. Edge ratio (mean MFE / mean MAE over 12 bars) falls from 1.9–2.4 at 02:00–04:30 UTC to 0.91–1.07 at 11:30–13:30. Aggregated to six windows and measured across 12 independent cells (2 markets × 2 sides × {disc_h1, disc_h2, validation}), the break-even queue probability q* in the 11:30–14:30 window is 0.58, 0.60, 0.60, 0.66, 0.67, 0.73, 0.88, 0.94, 0.95, 1.11, 1.21, 1.22 — it is the worst of the six windows in 9 of 12 cells and above 1.0 (dead even with perfect fills) in 4 of them. EV per fill under the optimistic touch-fill assumption in that window averages +0.13 ticks versus +0.55 everywhere else. The best windows are 07:00–11:30 UTC (q* 0.05–0.81, median 0.30) and 22:00–24:00 UTC (q* 0.06–0.61, median 0.25), then 02:30–07:00 UTC (median 0.31).
findings.markets: ZB and ZN
findings.economic_why: 08:30 US Eastern is when the US macro calendar prints — CPI, payrolls, PPI, claims, retail sales — and 12:30/13:30 UTC is that instant under EDT/EST respectively. Treasuries are the primary expression vehicle for rate expectations, so the entire informed flow of the day arrives in ZB and ZN in that window. A resting limit order in front of an informational shock is definitionally on the wrong side: it fills precisely because someone who knows more is taking the other side, and the bar keeps going. This is textbook adverse selection with an identifiable, calendar-driven counterparty, which is why it is the most reliable finding in this study and the one least likely to decay. The mirror image is that the Asian and early-European hours have almost no informed flow in the bond complex — just position adjustment and hedging — so passive fills there are benign.
findings.exit_evidence: In the toxic window, mean MAE over 12 bars is 6.1–8.5 ticks against a 12-tick stop, so a meaningful fraction of positions taken there run to the stop; p(stop) roughly triples relative to quiet hours. In the benign windows MAE12 is 1.4–2.2 ticks, i.e. the 12-tick stop is essentially never reached and the position is exited by the +2 target within 3–5 bars. This is why the same target/stop geometry that is comfortable overnight is dangerous at 12:30 — the exit structure is unchanged but the distribution it sits in is 4x wider.
findings.robustness: The direction of the effect is identical in ZB and ZN, on both the bid side and the offer side, and in disc_h1, disc_h2 and validation — 12 independent cells, all agreeing. Per-bucket cell sizes are 300–1,900 fills over 130–380 distinct days, so individual 30-minute buckets are noisy, but the six-window aggregation has 7,487–17,378 raw fills and 561–1,129 de-overlapped 24-bar episodes per cell. Applying the exclusion in the deployable sequential sim improves ZB net from +0.319 to +0.392 ticks per trade and ZN from +0.386 to +0.486 (touch-fill), while giving up ~18% of trades. The 13:00 UTC bucket is an oddity: good for the long side (q* 0.11/0.17) and bad for the short side (1.07/0.84); I have not resolved why and would not carve it out.
findings.tradeable_form: Hard calendar rule in the order router: cancel all resting quotes and do not place new ones between 11:30 and 14:30 UTC. Do not merely widen — the measurement says depth does not rescue this window (q* at depth 4 in that window is no better). Positions already open at 11:30 should be allowed to run their normal bracket; the finding is about entering, not holding. Optional refinement if slot pressure is low: also skip 05:30–06:00 UTC, the one other bucket where q* exceeds 0.6 in 3 of 4 market/side cells (ZB short 1.226, ZB long 0.906, ZN short 0.707, ZN long 0.614).

findings.title: The natural target is FIXED IN TICKS (2-3), not a multiple of volatility — the marginal value of one more tick of target turns negative between 3 and 4 ticks in every volatility regime
findings.observation: From a resting-limit fill in ZB/ZN, net-ticks-per-trade as a function of exit distance is a single-peaked curve that peaks at 2-3 ticks and declines monotonically thereafter. The peak does NOT move when volatility changes. Across five ATR quintiles whose median 5-min ATR spans 0.93 -> 3.36 ticks in ZB and 1.14 -> 3.57 ticks in ZN (a 3.6-3.8x range), the argmax target stays in {2,3} in 9 of 10 market x vol cells (the 10th, ZB atrq 0.2-0.4, has a flat top: T2=+0.550 vs T7=+0.586, a 0.036t difference = noise). Log-log slope of optimal target vs ATR = +0.28 (ZB, with the flat-top cell set to its plateau start) and +0.00 (ZN); 1.00 would mean 'scales with vol'. Marginal dNet/dT is positive T1->T2 in all 10 cells (+0.16 to +0.35t), roughly zero T2->T3 (-0.15 to +0.16t), and negative T3->T4 in 10 of 10 cells (-0.03 to -0.18t). ZN is the cleaner of the two: peak at T=2/3 with dNet/dT(3->4) negative in all five vol buckets. Separately, there is NO hazard collapse: P(MFE>=d+1 | MFE>=d) is flat at 0.866-0.871 from d=4 to d=13 ticks and then RISES to 0.89-0.90 beyond d=14. So the 2-3 tick optimum is not created by price 'stopping' at that distance; it is created by the interaction of a nearly memoryless excursion hazard with the fixed cost of the tail (time-exit slippage and the losing 11-19% of fills).
findings.markets: ZB, ZN (both sides; scaling verified in 5 ATR quintiles per market)
findings.robustness: argmax target in {2,3} in 9/10 market-x-volatility cells. ZN: T=3 peak in all 5 vol buckets (n_fill 8209/9590/10484/12537/15011; eps 702/1024/1138/1049/708), dNet/dT(3->4) negative in 5/5. ZB: T in {2,3} in 4/5 buckets (n_fill 5838-10684; eps 509-817). Also invariant to entry depth (1,2,3,4 ticks) and horizon (H=12,24,48,96): at every one of the 16 depth x horizon combinations in both markets the peak sits at T=2 or T=3. Holds on both the buy-limit and sell-limit side. Sub-buckets of the ZN QUIET cell (asia/eu/us, trend up/down, atrq lo/hi) all keep the same T=3 geometry with net +0.548 to +0.843t. The effect_ticks figure is the penalty for using a volatility-scaled target instead: in the top vol quintile, T=3 vs T=7 (~2x ATR) is +0.312 vs +0.136 in ZB (+0.176t) and +0.367 vs +0.010 in ZN (+0.357t).
findings.economic_why: This is a liquidity-provision payoff, not a forecast. The counterparty is whoever needed immediacy in the 5-6 bars after the reference close and paid the spread to get it. The provider's revenue is the price improvement on the fill, and it is collected almost immediately — 46% of the eventual T=3 hits arrive within 6 bars (30 min) and the median winning hold is 9 bars. Waiting past 3 ticks stops being paid for immediacy and starts taking directional risk, which the flat-then-rising hazard says is a fair-or-worse bet. Because the payoff is a spread capture and not a volatility capture, the optimum is anchored to the tick grid, which is why it does not scale with ATR. This is also the mechanism behind the exponent: the recovery/adverse geometry scales as ATR^0.45 while the target does not scale at all, so in high volatility the whole structure gets worse for the provider (net at best target falls from +0.72/+0.80 in mid-vol to +0.31/+0.37 in top-vol).
findings.exit_evidence: MFE/MAE from fill (ZN QUIET buy, n=12653): MFE p10=2 p25=3 p50=6 p75=10 p80=11 p90=16 p95=22, mean 7.88t; MAE p10=0 p25=2 p50=4 p75=8 p80=10 p90=14 p95=19, mean 6.34t; edge_ratio 1.242. Note MFE p50=6 is DOUBLE the optimal target of 3 — the median fill goes well past the optimal exit, and taking that extra distance still loses money because the paths that fail to reach it lose far more. Timing: P(T=3 hit by bar k) = 0.062/0.125/0.182/0.313/0.460/0.615/0.738 at k=1/2/3/6/12/24/48. Target hit rate 0.808, stop rate 0.008, time-exit rate 0.184, median hold 9 bars.
findings.tradeable_form: Exit geometry only (this finding sets the target, not the entry): after a resting-limit fill, place the profit-taking limit 2 ticks away in ZB and 3 ticks away in ZN, and do NOT widen it when volatility rises. Time-flatten at 48 bars or the EOD bar, whichever comes first. Both arms of this choice are limit exits paying identical commission, so the 0.27t improvement is captured at zero marginal cost — which is why clears_cost is true against a 0.0 differential floor.

findings.title: There is no expectancy-justified stop anywhere between 3 and 24 ticks — net P&L rises monotonically as the stop widens — but P(recovery) crosses 50% at ~3-4x the 5-min ATR, and that ratio is a near-universal constant across markets
findings.observation: Two separate measurements. (1) Sweeping the stop from 3 to 24 ticks to none, net ticks per trade increase monotonically in essentially every state tested, in both markets, on both sides. ZN QUIET at T=3: S3=+0.251, S4=+0.379, S6=+0.532, S8=+0.603, S12=+0.686, S16=+0.734, S24=+0.811, no-stop=+0.795. ZB QUIET at T=2: S3=+0.285, S4=+0.376, S6=+0.451, S8=+0.482, S12=+0.452, S16=+0.523, S24=+0.577, no-stop=+0.583. Tightening from S=24 to S=3 costs 0.560t (ZN) and 0.292t (ZB) per trade. (2) The recovery curve, measured fill-model-independently from plain bar closes: conditional on adverse excursion first reaching -a ticks, P(price later returns to the entry price within the window) is ZB a2:0.864 a3:0.748 a4:0.641 a5:0.552 a6:0.479 a8:0.375 a12:0.240 a16:0.164 and ZN a2:0.892 a3:0.774 a4:0.661 a5:0.565 a6:0.484 a8:0.370 a12:0.240 a16:0.186. The 50% crossing sits at 5.71t (ZB) and 5.80t (ZN). Crucially, holding beats stopping in expectation at EVERY adverse level measured: conditional on having been -24 ticks underwater, the T=2 no-stop policy still finishes at only -6.14t in ZB, versus -24.5t if you had stopped there. Third, the crossing point scales SUB-PROPORTIONALLY with volatility: log-log slope of the 50%-recovery distance vs ATR is +0.49 (ZB) and +0.44 (ZN), i.e. roughly sqrt(ATR). In ATR units the crossing falls from 4.36 ATR in the calmest quintile to 2.36 ATR in the wildest (ZB) and 3.93 -> 2.13 ATR (ZN). So high-volatility regimes are RELATIVELY less mean-reverting even though they are absolutely wider.
findings.markets: ZB, ZN primary; the a50/ATR ratio also measured in ZF, ZT, CL, 6E, ZC
findings.robustness: Stop-widening monotonicity holds in 22 of 24 state x market x side S-curves measured (the two exceptions are ZB trend_dn where S=8 beats S=24 by 0.010t, and ZN sess-us where S=12 beats S=24 by 0.016t — both inside noise). Recovery curves are near-identical across markets at matched states: ALL 5.71t (ZB) vs 5.80t (ZN); QUIET 4.81 vs 5.01; lowest vol tercile 4.35 vs 4.74; highest vol tercile 7.20 vs 7.06. The a50/ATR ratio measured on the QUIET state in every affordable market that could be resolved: ZB 3.74, ZN 3.50, ZF 3.94, ZT 3.79, CL 3.46, 6E 3.92, ZC 4.05 — a range of only 3.46-4.05 across four asset classes. (ES/GC/YM/RTY/HG returned no crossing because their ATRs are 6.6-12.1 ticks and my adverse grid stopped at 20 ticks = under 2 ATR; that is a grid limitation, not a finding.) Sub-buckets: measured separately in QUIET/BUSY, atrq terciles and asia/us sessions with 2525-19262 reaching events per cell.
findings.economic_why: The provider's position after a limit fill is short immediacy; the adverse excursion is the market continuing to demand the same side. Because the flow is overwhelmingly uninformed at these horizons, the position reverts more often than not, so any stop converts a recoverable drawdown into a realised loss — and does so while paying an extra 0.5 tick of market-order slippage. There is therefore no price at which a stop pays for itself in expectation. The sub-proportional ATR scaling has a clean reading: as volatility rises, more of the flow is information-driven, so a given number of ATRs of adverse movement is less likely to be noise and more likely to be a real repricing. That is the same adverse-selection gradient that shows up in the QUIET-vs-BUSY split in Finding 3.
findings.exit_evidence: The no-stop policy's loss tail is what forces a stop despite the expectancy: ZB T=2 no-stop has p5=-9.14t, p1=-24.14t, p0.1=-55.59t, min=-87.14t = -$2,723 on a ~$4,100 account. ZN is milder: p1=-21.29t, min=-83.29t = -$1,301. So the stop is a risk-of-ruin instrument, not an expectancy instrument, and the S-curve prices exactly what it costs. Placing it at 24 ticks costs 0.016t vs no stop in ZN QUIET (it actually gained 0.016t) and 0.006t in ZB QUIET, while capping the worst case at -24.5t = -$383 (ZN) / -$766 (ZB). Placing it at 6 ticks — right at the 50%-recovery landmark — costs 0.28t (ZN) / 0.13t (ZB), which is a third to a half of the entire edge.
findings.tradeable_form: Stop at 24 ticks (market order, budget 0.5 tick slippage) — wide enough that it costs ~0.01-0.02 ticks of expectancy and rarely fires (stop rate 0.008-0.018 in the headline cells) while capping the single-trade loss at ~$383 in ZN and ~$766 in ZB. Do NOT use a stop at the 50%-recovery distance (~6 ticks) despite its intuitive appeal: it costs 0.28t in ZN, roughly a third of the edge. With 4-5 concurrent 1-lot positions the worst-case simultaneous drawdown on a 24-tick stop is ~$1,900 (ZN) — sizeable but survivable on $4,100; ZB at ~$3,800 is not, so ZB requires either a tighter stop (and a materially smaller edge) or fewer concurrent positions.

findings.title: Limit fills in the QUIET state (5-min volume below 0.7x its trailing-day median AND bar range below 1.0 ATR) show favourable excursion asymmetry — edge_ratio 1.242 vs 1.145 unconditional — and the honest way to price it is f*, the break-even touch-only fill rate, which is 0.086 in ZN
findings.observation: The single most replicated conditioning axis is ACTIVITY, not direction. Sorting by 5-min volume relative to its own trailing-day median: net ticks per trade on the (limit -2t, T=argmax, S=24) policy is +0.534 (ZB) / +0.704 (ZN) when volume < 0.7x median, versus +0.284 (ZB) / +0.337 (ZN) when volume > 1.5x median. Same direction for bar range (<0.7 ATR: +0.538/+0.590; >1.5 ATR: +0.233/+0.310) and for ATR percentile (top quintile collapses to +0.097/+0.229 from +0.52-0.76 in the middle quintiles). Combining volume and range into the QUIET mask gives ZN buy-side: n_fill 12653, 1439 episodes, 459 days, P(touch)=0.477, net +0.811t CI95 [+0.647,+0.984], edge_ratio 1.242, MFE mean 7.88t vs MAE mean 6.34t. Critically, I then tested queue realism by requiring price to trade THROUGH the limit by 1 tick before counting a fill. This is the pessimistic bound and it flips the sign: ZN QUIET goes +0.811 -> -0.143t, ZB QUIET +0.577 -> -0.472t. Decomposing, the merely-TOUCHED (not traded-through) fills earn +1.912t (ZN) and +1.826t (ZB), while the traded-through fills earn -0.143t and -0.472t. The break-even fraction f* of touch-only limits you must actually get filled on is therefore 0.086 in ZN QUIET and 0.308 in ZB QUIET, versus 0.373/0.485 for the unconditional state and 0.608/0.628 for the BUSY state. This measurement also says the library's ADVERSE_BUFFER of 0.5 ticks understates the true touch-vs-through adverse-selection cost, which I measure at 0.95-1.13 ticks.
findings.markets: ZN (primary, f*=0.086); ZB (secondary, f*=0.308, less stable)
findings.robustness: ZN QUIET buy, touch-fill model: disc-H1 +0.771t (n=6371, eps=726), disc-H2 +0.851t (n=6282, eps=713), untouched VALIDATION split +0.822t (n=2971, eps=431). f* by split: 0.080 / 0.092 / 0.160. Context breakdown all positive and consistent: asia +0.757 (f*=0.127), eu +0.843 (f*=0.080), us +0.548 (f*=0.334), trend-up +0.815 (f*=0.068), trend-down +0.807 (f*=0.104), low-ATR half +0.816 (f*=0.067), high-ATR half +0.799 (f*=0.130). Misalignment null (QUIET index set circularly day-shifted, policy held fixed, 200 draws): real +0.811t vs null mean +0.598t, sd 0.086, z=+2.49, beats p95. Note the null mean is high because the policy itself works at arbitrary times — the STATE contributes only the +0.213t difference, not the whole +0.811t. FAILURES: the SELL side fails the misalignment null in both markets (ZN sell +0.515t vs null +0.456t, z=+0.67; ZB sell +0.436t vs null +0.426t, z=+0.12), and ZB's split-half is unstable (f* = 0.117 in H1 but 0.497 in H2). Depth scan in ZN QUIET: f* = 0.150/0.086/0.104/0.064 at depths 1/2/3/4 with edge_ratio rising 1.225/1.242/1.265/1.260 — consistent with the incumbent finding that edge_ratio rises with depth.
findings.economic_why: QUIET is defined by low volume and a compressed bar, which is precisely the state in which the order flow arriving at your limit is least likely to be informed. You are paid the spread by someone rebalancing or hedging into a thin, uneventful tape. The BUSY state is the mirror image — high volume means someone is working real size, your limit gets filled exactly when the market is about to keep going, and f* jumps to 0.61-0.63. The state and the queue work in the same direction, which is the load-bearing point: QUIET is low-volume, so the resting queue at each level is SHORT, so the realised touch-only fill rate f should be HIGH — at the same time as the required f* is LOWEST. That double alignment is why this cell is the only one worth deploying. It also means the edge self-limits: it exists only where there is little volume to trade against, so it does not scale.
findings.exit_evidence: MFE from fill p10=2 p25=3 p50=6 p75=10 p80=11 p90=16 p95=22 (mean 7.88t); MAE p10=0 p25=2 p50=4 p75=8 p80=10 p90=14 p95=19 (mean 6.34t); edge_ratio 1.242 vs 1.145 for all-bars fills. The asymmetry is real but modest and sits almost entirely in the left tail of MAE (p10=0, i.e. 10%+ of fills never trade against you at all). Optimal exit from the T-grid is 3 ticks; stop at 24 ticks per Finding 2; hit rate 0.808, stop rate 0.008, time-exit rate 0.184, median winning hold 9 bars, P(hit by bar 6)=0.313. Realised P&L distribution: p5=-9.3t, p25=p50=p95=+2.7t (the target), min=-24.8t = -$387.
findings.tradeable_form: ZN only. At each 5-min close where volume < 0.7x its trailing 288-bar median AND (high-low) < 1.0x ATR(14), rest a BUY limit 2 ticks below the close with a 6-bar TTL. On fill: profit-taking limit +3 ticks, protective stop -24 ticks (market, budget 0.5 tick slip), time-flatten at 48 bars or the EOD bar. Do not trade the sell side (fails the null). Expect ~3.1 non-overlapping episodes per day and a ~48% touch rate. THIS DOES NOT CLEAR THE STATED COST FLOOR AS WRITTEN: +0.811t is below the library's 0.938t nominal ZN floor, and under a strict trade-through fill assumption it is -0.143t. What it does clear is the f* test — you need only 8.6% of merely-touched limits to fill, versus 37% unconditionally and 61% in busy conditions. The correct next step is NOT more backtesting; it is to measure the bot's own realised touch-only fill rate live in ZN quiet conditions. If measured f > 0.16 the cell is live (at f=0.5 it pays $7.47 per fill); if f < 0.086 it is dead. No amount of further offline work can resolve this, because the answer is not in 5-min OHLCV.

findings.title: ZB and ZN 5-minute paths travel measurably LESS far than a reshuffling of their own bars at distances of 2-16 ticks, but conditional on having already travelled 5+ ticks they extend MORE — short-range compression, long-range extension
findings.observation: I built a bar-shuffle null: each forward bar is reduced to three offsets from the previous close (high, low, close), and the ORDER of those triples is permuted. This preserves the window's realised volatility, its bar-range distribution and every discretisation and censoring artefact exactly; only the sequence dies. Real running-max survival S(d) is below the shuffled null at every distance from 2 to 20 ticks, with the deficit peaking at 6-12 ticks: ZB ratio 0.928/0.924/0.929/0.926 at d=6/8/10/12; ZN 0.904/0.904/0.902/0.908. The deficit closes by d=24 (ZB ratio 1.008). Second, the conditional race: given price touched +u before -u, P(it reaches +2u before returning to the entry price) versus the same statistic on the bar-shuffled paths. At u=2 the real market round-trips MORE than the shuffle (ZB 0.366 vs 0.394, delta -0.027, se 0.003; ZN 0.325 vs 0.366, delta -0.041, se 0.0025). At u>=4 the sign flips and the real market extends MORE (ZB u=6 0.461 vs 0.411, delta +0.050; u=10 0.493 vs 0.446, delta +0.047; ZN u=8 0.462 vs 0.400, delta +0.063; u=10 0.483 vs 0.428, delta +0.055). The crossover is at u=3, where delta is +0.002 (ZB) and -0.008 (ZN). The two results reconcile: short-range reversion kills most excursions before they get going (hence lower S(d) overall), but the ones that survive past ~4-5 ticks are genuinely trending.
findings.markets: ZB, ZN (both sides)
findings.robustness: ZB n=59086 full 48-bar windows, 1362 episodes, 350 days; ZN n=79333, 1816 episodes, 463 days. Both markets show the same sign pattern at every u from 2 to 10, and independently on the long and short side (4 independent sign-sequences, all matching). Binomial se on the real decided sample is 0.0025-0.0057, so the u=2 reversion delta is 9-16 se and the u>=6 extension delta is 12-17 se on raw counts — though these are raw-count sigmas on overlapping windows, so treat them as ordering evidence rather than calibrated p-values. Sensitivity check: rerunning the race with the touch bar INCLUDED rather than excluded changes all levels sharply (u=2 real p_ext drops to 0.17/0.10) but preserves the real-vs-shuffle sign pattern at every u, confirming the comparison is artefact-free. Also cross-checked against an IID-return-bootstrap null which gave the same qualitative answer but is confounded by volatility clustering, which is why the bar-shuffle is the null I trust.
findings.economic_why: Short-range compression at 2-3 ticks is the mechanical footprint of two-sided liquidity provision: resting size at the inside levels absorbs and reverses small pushes. That is the same phenomenon Finding 3 monetises, seen from the path side rather than the P&L side. Long-range extension past 4-5 ticks is what happens when a push exhausts the resting book — once the provider inventory at those levels is gone, there is nothing to reverse the move, so it runs. The crossover at u=3-4 ticks is therefore a measurement of how deep the effective two-sided book is in these contracts, and it is essentially the same distance as the natural target in Finding 1 (2-3 ticks). Those two numbers agreeing from completely independent measurements is the strongest internal evidence I have that both are real.
findings.exit_evidence: This finding says explicitly that you CANNOT trade the long-range extension. At every u tested, the real p_extend is at or below 0.500 (ZB max 0.493 at u=10; ZN max 0.502 at u=12), which is the exact indifference point for a 'target 2u, stop at entry' trade. So even though the market extends more than a shuffle of itself, it never extends enough to make trailing a winner profitable against a breakeven stop. Combined with the flat MFE hazard (0.866-0.871 for d=4..13), the message is: take the 2-3 ticks, do not scale out, do not trail. Note the censoring caveat — the unresolved fraction rises from 0.00 at u=2 to 0.51 at u=10, so the high-u numbers are conditioned on a decided subset.
findings.tradeable_form: Not directly tradeable — this is structural evidence, and I am reporting it as such (clears_cost=false, effect_ticks=0.0). Its operational content is prescriptive-negative and it constrains the other three findings: (a) do not build a breakout or continuation entry at any distance from 2 to 16 ticks in ZB/ZN, because p_extend never reaches 0.500; (b) do not trail or pyramid a limit-provision winner; (c) the 3-4 tick crossover independently corroborates the 2-3 tick target of Finding 1 and should be treated as the ceiling on any exit distance in these two contracts.

findings.title: The limit-order 'liquidity provision' edge is a fill-price artifact: the fills you are GUARANTEED to get lose ~0.8 ticks, the fills that make money are the ones you probably don't get
findings.observation: Split every touch-fill into two physically distinct populations. (a) THROUGH: the bar's extreme traded strictly beyond your limit price, so you are certain to be filled. (b) TOUCH-ONLY: the bar's extreme is exactly your limit price, so you fill only if you are near the front of the queue. In ZB at depth 2 with a 3-tick target / 9-tick stop, THROUGH fills are 33% of touches and net -0.830 ticks (se 0.093, z -8.9); TOUCH-ONLY fills are 67% and net +0.969 ticks (se 0.073). ZN: THROUGH 32%, net -0.705 (se 0.078); TOUCH-ONLY 68%, net +1.051 (se 0.054). Equivalently: conditioning on price reaching level X, the 12-bar-forward close sits about 0.5-0.6 ticks ABOVE X but about 0.45-0.5 ticks BELOW X+1tick. So the entire apparent profit is the difference between your fill price and the local extremum, and it evaporates the instant you assume the market has to trade through you. The break-even queue fill-rate on touch-only bars is q=0.43 (ZB long), 0.44 (ZB short), 0.31 (ZN long), 0.36 (ZN short). Below that fill rate the whole book is a loser. Long and short are near-identical here (gap <=0.03 ticks), so this is not a directional statement, it is the price of standing in the queue.
findings.markets: ZB, ZN primary; same decomposition run in ES and GC
findings.robustness: ZB THROUGH net by bracket shape: T2S10 -0.678, T3S9 -0.761, T4S8 -0.822, T6S6 -1.029, T8S8 -1.056, T12S12 -1.263 (long); short within 0.22 t of long everywhere. By depth 1/2/3/4/6/8: -0.715/-0.761/-0.849/-0.942/-1.092/-1.296 -- monotonically WORSE with depth, i.e. deeper limits are more adversely selected, not less. ZN identical shape (-0.633 to -1.086). Negative in all 60+ state x side cells tested in both markets (see negative_results 8), z from -0.14 to -13.5. ZB validation split same sign: ATR-bracket through-fill net -0.59 to -1.06 t. Same-bar target/stop tie ambiguity is 0.2-2.7% of fills, so the conservative tie rule is not driving it.
findings.economic_why: Fully believable and it is the standard one. A resting bid is a free option written to the flow. When information arrives the market trades through you and you own the loser; when nothing arrives the market tags your price and leaves, and the queue in front of you (hundreds of lots at a ZB/ZN tick) absorbs the trade so you never got that fill. The 1.8-tick spread between the two populations IS the option premium the market charges you, and it is priced almost exactly at the value of the price improvement you were trying to harvest. There is no counterparty who loses -- this is the market correctly pricing queue priority, which a 1-lot retail order arriving last does not have.
findings.exit_evidence: Exit shape barely matters and the ordering is fixed: tighter targets lose least (T2S10 -0.678) and wider targets lose most (T12S12 -1.263), because a wide target just holds the adversely-selected position longer. p_target on the through-fills is 0.66-0.69 for T3S9 -- you win most trades and still lose money, which is the classic adverse-selection tell. Median duration 5-6 bars for T3S9. MFE/MAE on through-fills: edge_ratio drops to 0.835-0.966 (below 1) versus 1.06-1.19 for touch-fills.
findings.tradeable_form: NOT tradeable as stated. The operational form is a decision rule, not a strategy: before deploying ANY resting-limit book in ZB/ZN, measure the bot's own realised fill rate on bars where the market tags the limit price and does not trade through. If that measured rate is below 0.43 in ZB / 0.31 in ZN, the book is negative-expectancy by construction and no amount of state selection fixes it (60+ states tested, none positive). This is cheap to measure live with the existing bracket engine by logging, for every limit fill, whether the fill bar's extreme went beyond the limit price.

findings.title: In ZB/ZN calm volatility, DEEP down-spikes get bought back but deep up-spikes do not fade: a 1.1-1.8 tick long-minus-short gap at limit depths 5-8 that holds in both discovery halves and then flips out of sample
findings.observation: Rest a limit 5-8 ticks away from the close (TTL 6 bars) in calm volatility (ATR below its trailing-month mean) and require the market to trade through you, then bracket at 6 ticks target / 18 ticks stop. In ZN discovery the long leg (deep buy limit, filled on a spike down) nets -0.445/-0.514/-0.472/-0.365 ticks at depths 5/6/7/8, while the short leg (deep sell limit, filled on a spike up) nets -1.539/-1.921/-2.033/-2.177. The gap widens monotonically with depth: +1.093 (z+2.38), +1.407 (z+2.33), +1.561 (z+2.08), +1.811 (z+1.93). ZB shows the same shape at lower power: +0.733/+1.180/+0.980/+0.969 (z +1.26/+1.61/+1.11/+0.96). At shallow depths (1-3 ticks) the gap is ~0 in both markets, so this is specifically about how the market treats large, fast dislocations in a quiet tape, not a general direction preference. Critically the long leg is still NEGATIVE everywhere -- the asymmetry is real but sits entirely below zero.
findings.markets: ZN (strongest), ZB (same sign, weaker); not tested in ES/GC at these depths
findings.robustness: ZN discovery split-halves at depth 6: H1 gap +1.575 (z+1.91, n 867/943), H2 gap +1.226 (z+1.38, n 752/962) -- same sign, similar size, so it is not one regime. ZB depth 6 halves: H1 +0.570 (z+0.52), H2 +1.663 (z+1.72) -- same sign but H1 is noise. VALIDATION FLIPS: ZB depth 5 gap -0.882 (z-0.80, n 431/363), ZN depth 5 gap -0.712 (z-0.48, n 294/289); depths 6-8 in validation are UNDERPOWERED (<250 fills) and were not reported. Validation power is far too low to call this either way -- 76-84 distinct days. Cross-market agreement in discovery is the main support; out-of-sample confirmation is absent.
findings.economic_why: A plausible story exists for the discovery sample: 2023-12 to 2025-05 was a period in which quiet-tape sharp selloffs in Treasuries were repeatedly bid back (dip-buying / flight-to-quality demand), while quiet-tape sharp rallies were not symmetrically sold. The counterparty would be forced/stop-driven sellers hitting through a thin calm-vol book. But this is exactly the kind of story that is indistinguishable from 'bonds happened to behave that way for 18 months', and the validation flip is consistent with the story being sample-specific rather than structural. I do not believe it at deployment strength.
findings.exit_evidence: At depth 6 T6/S18 the long leg reaches its 6-tick target on 55.1% (ZN) / 55.9% (ZB) of fills versus 51.2% / 50.0% for the short leg. Wide stop is doing real work: at T3/S9 the same cells show gaps of only +0.15 to +0.37, so the asymmetry lives in the tail of the recovery, not the first few ticks. Suggests, if pursued, a target around 6 ticks and a stop of 15-20 ticks with a 90-bar time cap.
findings.tradeable_form: NOT deployable now. If someone wants to pursue it: ZN, calm-vol bars only (ATR below trailing-21-day mean), BUY limit resting 6 ticks below the bar close with 6-bar TTL, bracket +6 / -18 ticks, 96-bar time exit. That fires ~1619 times over 289 discovery days (~5.6/day, well inside the 4-5 concurrent-position budget) and nets -0.51 ticks (-$8/trade). It must first be shown that the long leg alone can be pushed above zero -- the +1.4 tick number is a long-minus-short spread, and you cannot trade a spread between two things you would never both do.

findings.title: ES has a stable negative-excursion skew that runs OPPOSITE to its drift: the market drifts up but the 48-bar downside excursion is consistently larger than the upside
findings.observation: From any bar close in ES, over the next 48 bars the mean maximum adverse excursion for a long (61.7 ticks) exceeds its mean maximum favourable excursion (57.3 ticks) -- edge_ratio 0.928 -- even though the mean 48-bar drift is +1.91 ticks UP. Measured from limit fills the same holds: at depth 3, long edge_ratio 0.936 versus short 1.083, and this ordering appears in every single cell measured. ZB and ZN show no such skew (long/short edge ratios within 0.06 of each other and both near 1.1); GC flips sign between halves and is not stable. So this is an ES-specific shape: the mean goes one way, the tail goes the other.
findings.markets: ES (stable); contrast ZB/ZN (absent), GC (unstable)
findings.robustness: Long/short edge_ratio at depth 3: discovery 0.936/1.083; discovery H1 0.981/1.040; discovery H2 0.910/1.111; VALIDATION 0.947/1.082. By session: asia 0.968/1.056, eu 0.906/1.125, us 0.934/1.082. By vol: calm 0.949/1.075, hot 0.927/1.089. Invariant across all 12 splits -- the most stable single asymmetry found in this whole assignment. It does NOT survive conversion to P&L: every ATR-scaled bracket (1x/1.5x/2x/1x-3x/3x-1x ATR) in both discovery and validation has SHORT strictly worse than LONG (S-L from -0.33 to -0.90), because the up-drift more than offsets the tail advantage.
findings.economic_why: Equity index negative skew -- up by the stairs, down by the elevator. Risk premium is earned slowly and paid back quickly; hedging and stop cascades make downside paths convex. This one has a genuine structural cause rather than a sample story, which is why it is stable across every split. But the counterparty question kills it as a trade: to monetise it you must be short in a market with positive expected return, so you are paying the risk premium to rent the tail.
findings.exit_evidence: The shape is a tail effect, not a drift effect: bars-to-first-touch of +/-1.5xATR is 8 up versus 7 down and P(up first) 0.4989 versus P(dn first) 0.4864 -- essentially symmetric timing. The difference lives in the magnitude of the extreme, not its speed. That argues for a very wide target and no stop-based exit, i.e. an option-like payoff, which a 1-lot futures bracket cannot express. The apparent 'shorts reach MFE faster' signal (median bars-to-MFE 20 short versus 25-26 long) is a drift artifact and should be ignored.
findings.tradeable_form: NOT tradeable in the current engine. It is a convexity observation, not a directional one, and every futures bracket that tries to harvest it loses (-1.69 to -2.94 ticks net, all cells, both splits). The only honest tradeable form would be a long-volatility / put-side expression, which this account has no access to. Record it as a market-structure fact that should be used to make ES LONG stops wider than ES SHORT stops if ES is ever traded, not as a signal.

findings.title: After a FAST adverse excursion (1xATR in 1-2 bars) forward realized volatility is ~8-13% above normal; after a SLOW one (12-23 bars) it is at or below normal. Universal across 8 markets.
findings.observation: Failure events were built with no strategy: at bar j, price's low (or high) crosses ref +/- 1.0 x ATR(ref), where ref is the highest (lowest) close of the trailing 24 bars at bar i, ATR taken at bar i (fully pre-move), refractory 24 bars. speed = j - i. I then measured mean TRUE RANGE over bars j+1..j+12 (failure bar EXCLUDED) divided by ATR(ref). Result, spike(speed 1-2) vs grind(speed 12-23) vs all-bar baseline: ZB 1.166 [1.133,1.202] / 1.091 [1.063,1.119] / base 1.082 [1.076,1.087]. ZN 1.164 [1.136,1.193] / 1.055 / 1.064. ES 1.188 / 1.148 / 1.098. GC 1.207 / 1.132 / 1.071. CL 1.196 / 1.129 / 1.071. 6E 1.191 / 1.144 / 1.076. YM 1.216 / 1.173 / 1.120. ZF 1.166 / 1.099 / 1.089. In 8/8 markets spike > grind and spike > baseline, with bootstrap CIs disjoint from baseline. During the failure itself TR/ATR is 1.17-1.24 for spikes vs 0.91-1.01 for grinds, so what is measured is the DECAY of that excess: roughly half of the spike's vol excess survives 12 bars forward. Price direction after the failure is separately measured and is nothing (see negative results).
findings.markets: ZB, ZN, ES, GC, CL, 6E, YM, ZF (all 8 tested)
findings.robustness: Split-half of discovery agrees in 8/8 markets (ZB spike h1=1.192 h2=1.139 vs grind h1=1.091 h2=1.091; ZN spike 1.171/1.156 vs grind 1.048/1.063; GC 1.230/1.184 vs 1.149/1.116; CL 1.195/1.196 vs 1.144/1.115; 6E 1.207/1.175 vs 1.129/1.159; YM 1.255/1.177 vs 1.173/1.174; ZF 1.168/1.164 vs 1.100/1.099; ES 1.183/1.194 vs 1.161/1.136 -- ES is the weakest, spike/grind only 1.035). Holds WITHIN session: ZN spike US 1.042 vs grind US 0.909 (ratio 1.146), spike nonUS 1.212 vs grind nonUS 1.115 (ratio 1.087); GC US 0.932 vs 0.887, nonUS 1.309 vs 1.230. There is a large session confound in the LEVEL (nonUS ratios run ~0.25 higher than US in every market because trailing ATR lags the US-open expansion) but the spike-vs-grind ORDERING survives inside both. n per cell 874-1475 raw (spike) and 2404-3513 (grind); episodes 380-686 and 873-1311. No misalignment null was run -- the statistic is a volatility ratio, not a signed drift, so the circular-shift null in core.py does not apply; the disjoint bootstrap CIs are the evidence instead.
findings.economic_why: Plausible: a 1xATR move compressed into 5-10 minutes is an inventory/liquidation event -- someone had to get out fast -- and the resulting order-book damage and follow-on hedging keeps ranges wide for the next hour. A 1xATR drift spread over two hours is ordinary two-way flow and leaves nothing behind. This is the standard vol-clustering asymmetry conditioned on move SPEED rather than move SIZE, and speed is precisely what the 5-min bar grid can see. I have no direct evidence of who loses; nobody has to lose for a vol-persistence fact to be true.
findings.exit_evidence: Not applicable as a directional trade. The excursion evidence says the extra vol is symmetric: pooled ZB+ZN limit fills at depth 2 after spike failures have mfe_p50 7.0 / mae_p50 6.0 ticks over 48 bars, versus 7.0 / 6.0 after grind failures -- i.e. BOTH tails widen equally and the edge_ratio is unchanged (1.113 spike vs 1.119 grind vs 1.129 baseline). There is no favourable excursion asymmetry to harvest.
findings.tradeable_form: NO TRADEABLE FORM FOUND, and I looked hard for one. The obvious hypothesis -- that wider forward ranges make deeper resting limits pay -- is FALSE: at spike-failure bars P(touch) at depth 3 rises only from 0.377 (baseline) to 0.388, and the touch-conditional 12-bar drift is +0.554 +/- 0.207 versus a baseline of +0.556 +/- 0.037. Identical. The only defensible use is as an EXECUTION/RISK input to strategies that already exist: for ~1 hour after a 1xATR-in-1-2-bars adverse excursion, expect per-bar true range ~1.08-1.13x ATR rather than ~1.0x, so a fixed-tick bracket is effectively ~10% tighter than intended and a fixed-tick stop is ~10% more likely to be hit. Concretely: in the live engine, tag bars where low <= max(close[-24:]) - 1.0*ATR14 (or the mirror) with speed <= 2, and for the next 12 bars either widen stops by ~10% or suppress new fixed-tick brackets. That is a sizing rule, not a signal.

findings.title: Providing liquidity IN THE DIRECTION of a slow 1xATR grind is measurably worse than providing it anywhere else; the penalty is real in both half-samples but the absolute level still sits under the cost floor.
findings.observation: Pooled ZB+ZN, pooling BOTH failure directions (which cancels any market-wide drift bias in the sample period), at failure bars I rested a limit 2 ticks away, ttl 6 bars, and measured the touch-conditional 12-bar drift from the fill. CONT = the limit is on the side that continues the failure move (sell limit above the close after a down-failure, buy limit below after an up-failure). REV = the mirror. After a GRIND failure (speed 12-23 bars): CONT = +0.331 +/- 0.120 ticks (n=3183 fills), REV = +0.661 +/- 0.120 ticks (n=3136). Difference -0.330 +/- 0.170. The all-bar direction-neutral baseline for the identical geometry is +0.559 +/- 0.027 ticks (n=63,635 fills), so the whole effect is CONT being 0.23 ticks WORSE than generic, not REV being better (REV is +0.10 over generic, i.e. nothing). The same pattern at depth 3: CONT +0.373 +/- 0.163, REV +0.671 +/- 0.169. After spike/fast/mid failures CONT and REV are indistinguishable (spike +0.610 vs +0.515; fast +0.615 vs +0.556; mid +0.586 vs +0.677 -- signs of the difference flip, all within 1 SE).
findings.markets: ZB + ZN pooled (both directions pooled). Not tested in other markets.
findings.robustness: Split-half of discovery is unusually clean for this cell: CONT h1 = +0.31, h2 = +0.35; REV h1 = +0.65, h2 = +0.67. Both halves agree to within 0.04 ticks, which is the only place in this whole investigation where a directional-ish asymmetry replicated across halves. Depth 3 reproduces the ordering (CONT +0.373 vs REV +0.671). Grind is also by far the biggest bucket (ZB 2404 + ZN 3124 failure bars, 873+1109 de-overlapped episodes, 301+399 distinct days), so it has the most power -- which is exactly why I distrust the smaller buckets rather than this one. NOT tested outside ZB/ZN and NOT run against the misalignment null (the pooled-direction construction makes the core.py circular-shift null ill-defined; a bespoke null would be the next step). Effective n for the pooled cell: episodes counted per market/side before pooling, 1994 total at H=48.
findings.economic_why: Weak but coherent: a slow 12-23 bar drift of 1xATR is what a real order-flow imbalance looks like -- a size seller working an order over two hours. Standing in front of it (selling above into a slow decline is fine; but joining it by resting a sell 2 ticks above the current price means you are the last seller into a market that has already been sold for two hours) means your fill is adversely selected by the same flow that caused the drift. The person on the other side of your CONT fill is the flow that has been right for two hours. I would not bet money on this story; the number is the evidence, the story is decoration.
findings.exit_evidence: 48-bar excursions from the fill are unremarkable and near-identical between CONT and REV (pooled ZB+ZN depth 2 at grind failures: mfe_p50 7.0, mae_p50 6.0 ticks, edge_ratio 1.119 vs baseline 1.119). There is no exit geometry that rescues the CONT side; it loses on the drift, not on the path. Median bars-to-MFE is not differentiated. Practically: nothing to exit into, because nothing should be entered.
findings.tradeable_form: This is an EXCLUSION FILTER for an existing liquidity-provision book, not a standalone trade. REV at +0.661 +/- 0.120 does not clear the ZB 0.794t / ZN 0.938t limit-entry cost floor, so trading it long is not available. What IS available: in the live engine, before placing a resting limit, compute d = (max(close[-24:]) - low) / ATR14 (and the mirror). If d >= 1.0 was first crossed 12-23 bars after the extreme bar, SUPPRESS limits placed on the continuation side of that move for the next ~12 bars. Expected saving vs placing them anyway: ~0.23 ticks per suppressed fill (~$7.2/fill in ZB, ~$3.6 in ZN). Whether that is worth the plumbing depends on how many of the incumbent book's fills land in this state -- I did not measure that overlap and it should be measured before anyone codes it.

findings.title: ZB/ZN limit "fills" are 67% zero-penetration touches, and those touches carry the entire apparent provision edge — required fill-probability q* exceeds 1.0 at the honest cost floor in every hour of every market tested
findings.observation: When a resting limit 2 ticks from the close is touched within 6 bars, I split the fills by how far price actually penetrated PAST the limit in the fill bar. ZB: 66.8% of fills are penetration=0 (the bar extreme equals the limit exactly and goes no further) and those carry +0.979 ticks at 12 bars with MFE/MAE 6.55/4.56 = 1.436. Penetration=1 carries +0.144. Penetration>=2 (13.0% of fills) carries -0.668/-1.428/-3.885 ticks with MFE/MAE collapsing to 0.84/0.74/0.52. ZN is identical in shape: pen=0 68.1% at +1.092 (ER 1.474), pen>=2 at -0.510/-1.280/-3.732. Consequence: the sign of passive market making is set entirely by whether a 1-lot at the back of the queue actually fills on an exact touch. Assuming it always does gives +0.474t (ZB) / +0.622t (ZN); requiring a 1-tick trade-through gives -0.534t / -0.364t. The gap is ~1.0 tick, which is exactly the assumed price improvement. Solving (q*SA+SB)/(q*NA+NB)=cost for the required exact-touch fill probability q*: ZB q*=3.59 and ZN q*=4.01 against the honest floor — impossible at any fill rate, because even q=1 (fill every single touch) yields 0.474 < 0.794 and 0.622 < 0.938. Against a commission-only floor (0.144t/0.288t, which ignores queue and stop slippage entirely) q*=0.408/0.389.
findings.markets: ZB, ZN primary; cross-checked in ZF, ES, YM, RTY, GC, CL, 6E, 6B, HG, ZC — best_case_clears_full is FALSE in all 12
findings.robustness: Bar-shuffle null (real bars permuted within UTC-hour buckets, preserving tick grid, intrabar geometry, bid-ask bounce and the diurnal profile; 6-8 seeds): the null itself produces +0.333t in ZB and +0.380t in ZN at depth 2 with touch fills. Real minus null = +0.140t (ZB, z=4.67) and +0.242t (ZN, z=14.24) — so genuine structure exists but is ~1/5 of the raw number. A synthetic tick-level random walk with a 1-tick spread and ZERO true edge reproduces +0.82t under touch fills and -0.20t under through fills, i.e. real ZB/ZN perform WORSE than a zero-edge random walk under both conventions. Full honest round-trip simulation (passive entry AND passive exit, stop as market order with 0.5t slip, timeout as market order with 1.0t slip, commission in ticks): thru=0 gives +0.28 to +0.41 t/trade pooled (t=14 to 46, 2675-3962 episodes); thru=1 gives -1.41 to -1.60 t/trade (t=-84 to -97). Sign flips entirely on the fill convention. Cross-market: E_touchfill is +0.463 ZF, +0.298 ES, +0.076 CL, +0.143 6E, and NEGATIVE in YM (-0.389), RTY (-0.284), GC (-0.289), HG (-0.085) — against floors of 1.23 to 4.25 ticks.
findings.economic_why: There is no counterparty story, because there is no edge to explain. The +0.47t is arithmetic: the fill price is 2 ticks below the reference close, and conditional on touching that level, price 12 bars later is on average 1.6 ticks BELOW the reference close. The market continues against the fill; the 2 ticks of assumed price improvement merely over-compensate. The only real question is whether you collect that improvement, and the pen=0 concentration says you collect it precisely on the occasions where a 1-lot at the back of a thin queue is least likely to trade. Whoever is on the other side of an exact-touch-and-bounce is the front of the queue, not you.
findings.exit_evidence: MFE/MAE conditional on fill quality is the cleanest exit signal here: pen=0 fills run MFE 6.55 / MAE 4.56 over 24 bars (ER 1.436), pen=4+ fills run 7.97 / 15.49 (ER 0.522). The distribution is bimodal on penetration, so any stop must be placed to eject the deep-penetration fills fast — but the bracket sim shows this does not rescue the economics: at depth 2 / target 2 / stop 6 with thru=0 the target hits 83% of the time and the stop 14%, and it still only nets +0.41t before the adverse-selection buffer. Widening to depth 3 / target 4 / stop 10 drops p_target to 0.63 and net to +0.28t.
findings.tradeable_form: None. This finding is a KILL, not a trade. The concrete instruction to the project: any backtest that fills a limit order when bar_low <= limit_price is inflating ZB by ~1.0 tick and ZN by ~1.0 tick per trade versus a trade-through rule, and the true value lies between. Every future limit-entry measurement must report both conventions, and the pen=0 share must be reported alongside. The incumbent's '+0.47 ticks at depth 2 after a 24-bar up-impulse in calm vol' is numerically indistinguishable from the UNCONDITIONAL depth-2 touch-fill value of +0.474 ticks measured on all 70,580 tradable ZB discovery bars — the impulse condition contributes nothing.

findings.title: Provision value has a stable, repeatable clock: ZB/ZN hours 03,04,11,18,22 UTC are worth 0.2-0.8 ticks more than hours 00,02,10,12,15 — real structure above the shuffle null, still short of the cost floor
findings.observation: Touch-conditional 12-bar value from a depth-2 limit fill, symmetrised over buy and sell, varies by a factor of 6 across the UTC clock and the pattern is the same in both markets. ZB best-case-fill value by hour: 04=0.733, 20=0.659, 22=0.648, 11=0.646, 18=0.632, 07=0.612 versus worst 00=0.080, 02=0.269, 06=0.319, 12=0.368. ZN: 20=0.950, 11=0.813, 16=0.747, 08=0.736, 23=0.723, 04=0.722 versus 12=0.471, 15=0.499, 00=0.502. Against the bar-shuffle null the excess at depth 3 is largest at hour 22 (ZB +0.802, z=4.36; ZN +0.839, z=5.12), hour 04 (ZB +0.555, z=2.66; ZN +0.570, z=2.64) and hour 11 (ZN +0.774, z=2.73). The quiet overnight hours are structurally the most generous to a liquidity provider and the US data hours (12,13,14,15 UTC) the least — hour 12 has the lowest pen=0 share (0.50 vs 0.86 at hour 04), i.e. when the market comes to your price during the US session it goes THROUGH it. Separately, the diurnal realized-range signature is sharp: the first 5-min bar after every session boundary runs 1.4-1.6x ATR (07:05 = 1.51x ZB / 1.40x ZN; 13:35 = 1.57x / 1.60x; 20:00 = 1.39x / 1.25x; 22:05 = 1.62x / 1.60x; 00:05 = 1.52x / 1.45x) and decays to below 1.0x within 30 minutes. Volume at 20:00 UTC is 4x baseline in ZB and 4x in ZN.
findings.markets: ZB, ZN
findings.robustness: Chronological split-half of discovery (2023-12 to 2025-05) on the best-case-fill value at depth 2: ZN hour 04 = 0.721 / 0.723 (the most stable cell measured anywhere in this campaign), ZN hour 03 = 0.648 / 0.651, ZB hour 03 = 0.570 / 0.607, ZB hour 18 = 0.601 / 0.660, ZB hour 22 = 0.617 / 0.680. UNSTABLE cells that would have been false positives on pooled data: ZB hour 11 = 1.076 / 0.231, ZB hour 07 = 0.793 / 0.430, ZN hour 22 = 0.785 / 0.512, ZN hour 23 = 0.942 / 0.507, ZB hour 12 = 0.122 / 0.621. Cross-market agreement on the good hours (03, 04, 11, 18, 22) and the bad hours (00, 12, 15) is strong. Honest round-trip at ZN hour 04, depth 2 / target 2 / stop 6, thru=0: +0.716 t/trade net of commission, t=15.0, 354 episodes on 354 distinct days, p_target 0.855, p_stop 0.082, p_fill 0.345. The same cell at thru=1 is negative. ZB hour 22, depth 3 / target 3 / stop 8, thru=0: +0.862 t/trade, t=5.98, but only 180 episodes and p_fill 0.177.
findings.economic_why: Plausible: in the 03:00-05:00 and 22:00-23:00 UTC windows the ZB/ZN book is thin and the flow is largely non-informed (Asian-hours hedging, position squaring, the Globex reopen rebuild). A provider is compensated for inventory risk rather than picked off. Conversely at 12:00-15:00 UTC the flow around US data releases is informed: the pen=0 share collapses from 0.86 to 0.50, which is the direct signature of being run over rather than bounced off. The story is believable and the pen=0 share is the measured mechanism, not an assumption. But the compensation is 0.72 ticks and the honest cost of standing there is 0.94 ticks — the market is charging correctly.
findings.exit_evidence: Hold horizon should be short: at ZN hour 04 depth-2 fills, MFE/MAE over 24 bars is 1.52 with a median bars-to-MFE well inside the window; the target-2/stop-6 bracket resolves 85.5% at target and only 8.2% at stop, so the useful exit is a 2-tick scratch-plus, not a runner. Widening the target to 3 with a stop of 8 drops net from 0.716 to 0.507 — the excursion does not extend. The overnight hours also have the smallest MAE tail: fwd 24-bar range at hour 04 in ZB is ~0.86 ticks of bar range, so a 6-tick stop is roughly 7 bar-ranges away and is almost never the binding constraint.
findings.tradeable_form: NOT deployable as measured. If a future campaign wants to re-test it after obtaining real fill statistics from the live bot: buy limit 2 ticks below the 5-min close and sell limit 2 ticks above, both resting with a 6-bar TTL, only during 03:00-05:00 and 22:00-23:00 UTC; on fill, exit limit 2 ticks in favour, protective stop 6 ticks, flatten after 24 bars. In ZN this is +0.72 ticks gross under the optimistic fill and -0.5 ticks under the conservative one. The gating measurement the project actually needs is empirical: log every resting limit the live bot places, record whether it filled when the tape merely touched its price, and estimate q directly. If measured q > 0.41 (ZB) / 0.40 (ZN) the strategy clears commission but still not the queue-adjusted floor.

findings.title: Compression predicts volatility expansion strongly and monotonically, but produces the SMALLEST absolute moves — calm is the worst place in the day to trade, not the best
findings.observation: Conditional on the current ATR percentile, measured causally, the ratio of ATR 24 bars later to ATR now is monotone: ZB 1.772 (atr_pct 0-0.05), 1.479, 1.285, 1.251, 1.148, 1.005, 0.852, 0.701 (atr_pct 0.95-1.0). ZN is nearly identical: 1.621, 1.389, 1.259, 1.197, 1.145, 1.004, 0.871, 0.676. So compression DOES lead to expansion — reliably, in relative terms. But the absolute forward 24-bar realized range moves the other way: ZB 6.52 ticks in the calmest 5% rising monotonically to 21.61 ticks in the wildest 5% (ZN 7.03 to 21.11). The p90 of the forward 2-hour range in the calmest bucket is 11 ticks; in the wildest it is 38. Expressed as range/current-ATR the calm bucket looks spectacular (9.4x vs 3.9x) and this is the trap — the multiplier is large only because the denominator is 0.69 ticks. Volume drought (volume < 0.3x trailing median, 17,364 ZB bars / 23,306 ZN bars) gives a forward 24-bar range of 7.41 / 7.43 ticks in the two markets against ATR of 1.20 / 1.42, i.e. the same picture from the volume side. Directionally, calm predicts nothing: ZB atr_pct<0.05 drift at 12 bars is -0.208 ticks (bar-shuffle z=-2.03), at 24 bars -0.311 (z=-2.02); ZN -0.121 (z=-1.17) and +0.002 (z=-0.88).
findings.markets: ZB, ZN
findings.robustness: The monotonicity holds across all 8 ATR-percentile buckets in both markets with no inversions, on 4,147-18,802 bars per bucket. Effective n for the calmest bucket is 308 episodes / 219 days (ZB) and 370 / 279 (ZN) at H=48 — powered. No misalignment null was run for this one because it is a descriptive conditional distribution rather than a directional prediction; the bar-shuffle comparison on the ATR-normalized forward range (z=-13.7) is confounded, since shuffling destroys volatility clustering by construction and therefore guarantees a large z that means only 'volatility clusters'. The absolute-ticks table needs no null: it is what it is. The directional component fails: |z| <= 2.03 against the bar-shuffle null and the effect is 0.1-0.3 ticks against a 0.79-0.94 tick floor.
findings.economic_why: This is volatility mean-reversion, which is real and universal, but it is not an inefficiency and nobody is on the other side losing. The tradeable content would be a straddle/breakout out of compression, and the number that kills it is 6.52 ticks of expected 2-hour range against ~1.6 ticks of round-trip cost for a two-sided breakout structure in ZB (two entries, one of which is wrong and must be stopped). In the wildest bucket the same structure faces 21.6 ticks of range against the same 1.6 ticks of cost. If the project wants range, it should trade the loud hours, not the quiet ones.
findings.exit_evidence: In the calmest 5% the p90 of the forward 24-bar range is 11 ticks (ZB) / 12 ticks (ZN) — so even the ninetieth-percentile outcome after maximum compression offers about 5 ticks of one-directional travel from a mid entry. Any target beyond ~4 ticks is in the tail. In the top 5% ATR bucket p90 is 38 / 36 ticks. Targets and stops must be scaled to the ATR bucket, not fixed.
findings.tradeable_form: Use as a SIZING/GATING filter, not a signal: atr_pct is a clean causal predictor of the absolute size of the next 2 hours' range, so any fixed-tick target/stop geometry should be indexed to it. Concretely, forward 24-bar range in ticks is well approximated by 4.0 to 6.7 times the current ATR in ticks with the multiplier falling as ATR rises; a target of 0.35x the current ATR-in-ticks-times-5 is roughly the median attainable move in every bucket. Do NOT trade compression breakouts in ZB/ZN.

findings.title: A weak, statistically solid FADE follows every kind of extreme in ZB/ZN — volume spikes, momentum, new day extremes — at 0.08 to 0.40 ticks, which is 2 to 10 times below the cost floor
findings.observation: Signing forward drift by the direction of the triggering event, everything reverts slightly, and nothing reverts enough. ZB volume > 8x trailing median (n=2,651, 657 episodes, 281 days): 6-bar drift -0.279 ticks, day-clustered t=-3.84; 12-bar -0.273 (t=-3.44); 24-bar -0.401 (t=-2.10). ZN volume > 4x median (n=12,230, 1,575 episodes): -0.118 (t=-3.57) / -0.099 (t=-2.89). Volume drought also fades: ZB -0.143 (t=-2.90), ZN -0.161 (t=-5.49). Trailing 6-bar momentum > 1.5x ATR: ZB 12-bar drift -0.105 (bar-shuffle z=-2.95), ZN -0.209 (z=-3.13). New day extreme after 48 bars: ZB -0.291 (z=-2.02), ZN -0.185 (z=-2.16). 24-bar momentum > 3x ATR at 48 bars: ZB -0.404 (z=-2.31), ZN -0.408 (z=-1.43). Every single one of these has the same sign in both markets. The largest single-bar events are the exception and are null: bar range > 4x ATR gives ZB -0.042 at 12 bars and ZN +0.598 (opposite signs, n=143 and 169 — UNDERPOWERED by the project's own raw<200 rule).
findings.markets: ZB, ZN
findings.robustness: Sign agreement across ZB and ZN on 5 of 6 extreme definitions. Day-clustered standard errors used throughout (naive SEs on overlapping 12-48 bar windows are inflated by roughly sqrt(H) — for day-of-week I measured this directly: the naive t on ZB Tuesday 48-bar drift was -6.0 and the day-clustered t was -1.42). Effective n is comfortable: 657-1,852 de-overlapped episodes on 281-462 distinct days. The bar-shuffle null (8 seeds) puts these at z = -2.0 to -3.1, so they are not artifacts of the diurnal profile or of intrabar geometry. They are simply too small: the largest is 0.40 ticks against a 0.79-tick floor in ZB and 0.94 in ZN, and using a market entry rather than a limit would raise the floor to 1.79 / 1.94 ticks.
findings.economic_why: Consistent with short-horizon inventory unwinding: a volume spike or a fast 6-bar move leaves a dealer with inventory to work off, and the price gives back a fraction of the move over the next 30-120 minutes. The counterparty is the momentum chaser. The story is believable, the direction is right, and the size is exactly what a competitive market would leave on the table — about a fifth of a tick, i.e. less than the cost of touching it.
findings.exit_evidence: For the largest of these (ZB volume>8x, 24-bar drift -0.401) the excursion profile gives no rescue: forward 24-bar realized range is 15.3 ticks against an ATR of 3.69, so the MAE distribution on a fade entry is wide relative to a 0.4-tick expectancy. Reversion after extremes is a small mean shift inside a large distribution, not a reliable path — there is no stop placement that converts a 0.4-tick mean into a positive expectancy after 0.79 ticks of cost, because the required stop-to-target ratio would have to exceed what the range distribution supports.
findings.tradeable_form: None standalone. Usable only as a directional TIE-BREAKER on a trade that is already justified: when otherwise indifferent between the two sides of a passive quote, lean the side that fades the last 6 bars of momentum. Expected contribution 0.1-0.2 ticks, which is real (z=-3.0) and free if it costs no extra transaction.

findings.title: The penetration law: forward drift after a limit fill is a monotone decreasing function of how far the bar traded PAST your limit — and it crosses zero at ~0.35 ATR of penetration in all 12 markets
findings.observation: Rest a buy limit below the close and split the fills by how far the fill bar's low went past the limit. Drift after the fill declines smoothly and monotonically with penetration, in every market tested, and the curve collapses onto ONE line when both axes are normalized by ATR. Pooled over 12 markets (983,599 fills), 12-bar drift in ATR units by penetration bucket: [0,0.05)ATR -> +0.541, [0.05,0.15) -> +0.381, [0.15,0.30) -> +0.260, [0.30,0.50) -> +0.064, [0.50,1.0) -> -0.220, >1.0ATR -> -0.896. MFE/MAE edge ratio tracks it exactly: 1.252, 1.186, 1.132, 1.013, 0.903, 0.691. In raw ZB ticks (buy limit 2 ticks below close, all bars): pen0 +0.971t (t=+10.7, 66.8% of fills), pen1 +0.070t (t=+0.5), pen2 -0.879t (t=-3.3), pen3 -1.981t, pen4+ -4.955t. This is not a liquidity payment. It is conditioning on a local extreme: 'the bar's low exactly equalled my price and never went lower' IS the definition of a local bottom, so of course price rises afterwards. Consequence: the ONLY bucket with edge_ratio>1 in the rates complex is the exact touch — precisely the fill you are least likely to actually receive, because your order sits at the back of a queue at a price that trades once and leaves. Universality check across the 96 all-bars cells (12 markets x 2 sides x 4 depths): exact-touch drift is positive in 96/96 (mean +3.65 ticks) and exact-touch edge_ratio >1 in 96/96 (mean 1.263); through-fill drift is positive in only 5/96 (mean -0.861) and through-fill edge_ratio >1 in only 18/96 (mean 0.936).
findings.markets: All 12 measured: ZB, ZN, ZF, ZT, ES, GC, CL, 6E, RTY, YM, NG, HG
findings.robustness: Monotonicity holds in 12/12 markets (the '6 of 12 strictly monotone' count is an artifact of two near-empty bins in ZB/ZF/ZT where the tick is 0.5-1.0 ATR wide; visually all 12 trace the same curve). frac_exact_touch correlates -0.992 with log(ATR in ticks) across markets — near-deterministic. Split by market: ZB 66.8% exact, ZN 68.3%, ZT 80.4%, ZF 60.0%, 6E 47.9%, NG 26.7%, CL 19.5%, HG 19.3%, ES 17.3%, RTY 10.6%, YM 10.6%, GC 10.1%. Break-even queue-fill probability q (fraction of exact touches you must actually be filled on) to merely cover commission, before any exit cost: ZB all-bars sell depth2 q=0.258, ZB buy depth2 q=0.562, ZB incumbent impulse_up_calm depth2 q=0.418, ZN incumbent depth2 q=0.386. A misalignment null was deliberately NOT used here — it is the wrong control for a within-fill conditioning artifact. The controls used instead are stronger: (a) the monotone penetration gradient, (b) the 12-market ATR-normalized collapse, (c) 96/96 vs 5/96 sign universality.
findings.economic_why: There is no counterparty story, and that is the point. Nobody is losing money to you in the exact-touch bucket — you are measuring a selection effect on the price path, not a transfer. The bar printed its low at your price and left; the volume that traded there was consumed by orders that were already resting ahead of you. To collect the +0.97 ticks you must be filled at a price where, by construction, minimal volume traded. The honest counterparty story runs the other way: on the through-fills, where you DO reliably get filled, someone is selling to you because they have a reason to keep selling, and your drift is -0.79 ticks. That is textbook adverse selection and it is the only regime you can actually reach.
findings.exit_evidence: Exit measurement makes it worse, not better. Full round-trip grid on ZB and ZN (810 cells: depth 1-3 x target 1/2/3/4/6 x stop 3/6/12 x hold 12/24/48 bars) at the MOST optimistic queue assumption q=1.0 (i.e. crediting every exact touch as a fill): ZERO cells positive net of commission + 0.5t stop slippage + 1.0t time-exit slippage. Best cell of 810 is ZN all-bars buy, depth2/target3/stop12/H48 = -0.266 ticks (t=-3.34, -$4.16/trade). No-stop pure-time-exit variant is also uniformly negative: best is ZB all-bars sell depth3 H48 = -0.170 ticks. Sensitivity to q on the incumbent ZB impulse_up_calm depth2/target2/stop4/H24: q=1.0 -> -0.342t (-$10.69), q=0.5 -> -0.665t, q=0.25 -> -0.911t, q=0.0 -> -1.296t (-$40.50). MFE/MAE confirms: edge_ratio for through-fills is 0.822-0.833 in ZB, i.e. adverse excursion exceeds favourable excursion.
