findings.tradeable_form: NONE. This finding is the reason not to trade, and it retires a class of measurement rather than proposing an entry. Concretely it invalidates any edge computed with core.touch_conditional()'s default fill rule (low <= limit counts as a fill), which is how the incumbent ZB +0.47-tick 'liquidity provision' edge was produced. Actionable instruction for the project: every future limit-entry claim must be reported at pen=0 AND pen=1, with the break-even q stated; a claim that survives only at pen=0 is a queue artifact, not an edge. If the project wants to keep pursuing liquidity provision it must first measure its OWN live fill rate on resting orders at prices that only touch — that single number (q) decides whether the entire research direction is viable, and it cannot be obtained from OHLCV.

findings.title: The rates complex reliably fades fast moves at every hour of the day — 0.11 to 0.44 ticks, which is real, survives every null, and is 3-8x too small to trade
findings.observation: After a 3-bar move of >=1.0 ATR in ZB/ZN/ZF/ZT, price gives part of it back over the next 6 bars (30 min). Measured as a signed fade (positive = reversion), pooled over 48 hour-cells in the four rates markets, 45/48 cells are positive. Thin hours (00:00-07:00 UTC): ZB +0.163t (t=+2.95), ZN +0.234t (t=+5.16), ZF +0.194t (t=+4.72), ZT +0.112t (t=+7.05). Thick US hours (13:30-20:00 UTC): ZB +0.149t (t=+2.00), ZN +0.208t (t=+2.63), ZF +0.221t (t=+2.34), ZT +0.098t (t=+2.27). The single largest cell anywhere is the 22:00-23:00 UTC reopen: ZB +0.429t (t=+2.93, 240 episodes), ZN +0.436t (t=+2.87, 299 episodes), ZF +0.375t (t=+1.93), ZT +0.155t (t=+2.15). Thinness matters, but only mildly: pooled regression across the 48 rates hour-cells gives fade = 0.162 - 0.034*log(volume_ratio), corr = -0.338; cells with volume below half the market median average +0.200 ticks vs +0.121 ticks for cells above 3x median. So this is a general rates-complex reversion that is modestly amplified when the book is thin — NOT a distinctive thin-hours participant effect. The effect is also strictly a same-direction-of-move phenomenon and is absent or reversed in the equity and commodity markets tested.
findings.markets: ZB, ZN, ZF, ZT (present in all four). Absent/inconsistent in ES, GC, CL, 6E, RTY, YM, NG, HG.
findings.robustness: Misalignment null (400 circular whole-day outcome shifts, day-clustered): ZB thin z=+3.24, ZN thin z=+4.36, ZF thin z=+2.65, ZT thin z=+7.05->z=+3.84; thick hours z=+2.40/+3.19/+2.49/+3.01. Beats null everywhere. Split-half (chronological): ZN thin h1=+0.232 / h2=+0.236 (near-identical); ZT thin h1=+0.081 / h2=+0.144; ZF thin h1=+0.151 / h2=+0.237; ZB thin h1=+0.233 / h2=+0.094 (weakest, still same sign). Day-clustered 95% CIs exclude zero in all four thin cells: ZB [+0.042,+0.258], ZN [+0.146,+0.325], ZF [+0.108,+0.272], ZT [+0.082,+0.146]. Effective n is genuinely large: 2811-3638 de-overlapped episodes over 294-391 distinct days. The four markets are highly correlated instruments on one curve, so this is closer to one observation replicated four ways than four independent confirmations — but the internal consistency (45/48 hour-cells positive) is strong.
findings.economic_why: Plausible and consistent with what was measured: a 1-ATR 3-bar move in a 1-2 tick-wide instrument is largely inventory pressure, not information. Whoever absorbed it wants out, and the curve arbitrages the four contracts against each other, so a dislocation in one tenor gets pulled back by relative-value flow. The amplification in thin hours (0.200 vs 0.121 ticks) fits: fewer resting participants means a given order pushes further past fair value before it stops. But the honest reading of the size is that this is exactly the residual the market makers leave on the table after they have taken their spread — 0.1-0.4 ticks is smaller than the bid-ask, which is why it survives. It is not a mispricing anyone is being punished for.
findings.exit_evidence: There is no exit that recovers it, and worse, a limit entry inverts the sign. Attempting to harvest the fade with a resting limit in the fade direction produces NEGATIVE through-fill drift because the fills are adversely selected toward the moves that kept extending: ZB T3_thin_fade_up through-fill depth1 12-bar = -0.586t (t=-2.73), ZN -0.597t (t=-3.04), ZT -0.679t (t=-3.28), ZF -0.314t (t=-1.62). Market-entry excursion is symmetric-to-slightly-favourable (edge_ratio 1.06-1.18) but the MFE is on the order of the effect size itself, leaving nothing after a 1-tick entry slip. Cost accounting: a market entry costs commission + 1.0t entry slip + 0.15t expected stop slip = 1.29t in ZB and 1.44t in ZN, against a 0.16-0.44t effect. Even charging commission ALONE (0.144t ZB, 0.288t ZN) and assuming a zero-slip limit in and a zero-slip limit out — physically impossible, and contradicted by the through-fill numbers above — the margin is 0.02-0.15 ticks, i.e. $0.60-$4.70 per round turn before a single adverse fill.
findings.tradeable_form: NOT TRADEABLE — report as REAL BUT UNTRADEABLE and stop. The effect is 0.11-0.44 ticks against an honest cost floor of 0.794t (ZB) / 0.938t (ZN) / 1.226t (ZF) / 0.938t (ZT), and against a market-entry cost of 1.29-1.73t. It fails by a factor of 3-8x, and the only entry mechanism cheap enough to reach it (a resting limit) flips the sign to -0.31 to -0.68 ticks through adverse selection. The one thing worth carrying forward is diagnostic, not directional: the 22:00-23:00 UTC reopen is where rates reversion is strongest (+0.43t in ZB and ZN), so if the project ever acquires an execution edge that lowers the cost floor below ~0.3 ticks, that hour is where to look first.

findings.title: ZB/ZN: passive quoting is materially worse for ~3 bars after an outsized 5-min bar (a suppression filter, not a trade)
findings.observation: When a ZB or ZN 5-min bar closes more than ~2.1-2.3x ATR14 away from the prior close (top 1% of bars, ~6 ticks, ~2 events/day), a limit order resting into the next few bars gets filled at a normal rate but the fill is then worse than an identical limit resting at a random time. The market does not go in a predictable DIRECTION afterwards - both the buy-limit-below and the sell-limit-above are hurt, roughly symmetrically. What changes is the shape of the path after the fill: adverse excursion grows much more than favourable excursion (ZB long d1 H=24: MAE 5.37 -> 6.09 ticks while MFE only 6.12 -> 6.30, so edge_ratio falls 1.140 -> 1.035; ZN short: 1.188 -> 0.990), the stop-out rate rises (ZB d1 T2/S4: p_stop 0.234 -> 0.319, p_target 0.736 -> 0.655) and net per fill falls. The penalty decays over about 3-4 bars: mean lift across ZB+ZN cells is k0 -0.541, k1 -0.486, k2 -0.501, k3 -0.345, k4 -0.088, k5 -0.044 ticks, after which it settles at a low residual of -0.15 to -0.28. Same-shaped penalty appears in ES/GC/CL/6E with fixed-tick brackets, but there it is entirely a volatility-scaling artifact (see robustness) - only in the treasury complex does it survive volatility correction.
findings.markets: ZB and ZN (primary, survives vol-correction). Measured but NOT surviving vol-correction in ES, GC, CL, 6E.
findings.economic_why: Believable and specific to the treasury complex. A >2x-ATR 5-min bar in ZB/ZN is almost always a scheduled-information event (13:30 UTC US data, auction results, Fed speakers) rather than a liquidity air-pocket. The counterparty who lifts your resting order in the minutes after such a print is disproportionately someone repricing on information you do not have, and the price keeps travelling. The reason this is NOT the same story in ES/GC/CL/6E is that in those markets a p99 5-min bar is far more often flow/liquidity driven, and once you resize the bracket to the new volatility the penalty disappears (ES +0.00/-0.00, 6E +0.08/+0.10 with a reactive sigma). The absence of a direction asymmetry (both sides equally hurt) is itself the tell: this is not a directional forecast, it is a widening of the two-sided distribution that a fixed bracket cannot absorb.
findings.exit_evidence: MFE/MAE from the fill over 24 bars, p99 vs all bars. ZB long depth1: MFE 6.30 vs 6.12, MAE 6.09 vs 5.37, edge_ratio 1.035 vs 1.140, MFE_p50 4 vs 4 ticks, MAE_p50 4 vs 3 ticks. ZB short depth1: ER 1.163 vs 1.163 (flat). ZN long depth1: MFE 7.59 vs 6.28, MAE 6.12 vs 5.24, ER 1.240 vs 1.199 - excursions BOTH get bigger, which is why a fixed 4-tick stop suffers while a sigma-scaled one suffers less. ZN short depth1: MFE 6.90 vs 6.28, MAE 6.97 vs 5.29, ER 0.990 vs 1.188 - clear deterioration. Exit-reason decomposition confirms the mechanism rather than a drift: ZB d1 T2/S4 p_stop 0.319 vs 0.234 baseline, p_target 0.655 vs 0.736. Destinations within 24 bars of the p99 bar are non-directional: 1xATR hit 0.79-0.81 and 2xATR hit 0.59-0.66 on BOTH sides in both markets, i.e. the market simply travels far in both directions. Implication for exits: if you must be in a position across such a bar, the stop must be sized to post-event volatility, not to the pre-event ATR14 - that alone removes most of the damage.
findings.robustness: 12 cells = {ZB,ZN} x {long,short} x {T3/S12/H48 d2, T4/S8/H24 d2, T2/S4/H24 d1}. Lift negative in 12/12 (range -0.972 to -0.178, mean -0.541). Split-half: negative in both chronological halves of discovery in 11/12 cells (only ZB T3S12 short H1 = +0.213). HELD-OUT VALIDATION (2025-06-21..2025-12-31, never used for selection): negative in 11/12 cells (only ZN T4S8 short = +0.142), values -0.258 to -1.044. Whole-day-shift misalignment null on the state mask: z = -2.19, -0.84, -3.49, -0.84, -5.00, -3.46, -2.67, -3.92, -2.38, -3.40, -5.69, -5.92 (median -3.44; the two weak cells are both ZB short). Fill-assumption invariance (the critical check): under the optimistic touch-fill the ZB long d1 lift is -0.547 and under the pessimistic trade-through fill it is -0.502, while the BASELINE LEVEL moves by 1.08 ticks (+0.217 -> -0.867) - so the lift is identified even though the level is not. Cross-market with fixed-tick brackets: p99+ lift negative in 36/36 cells across ZB, ZN, ES, GC, CL, 6E (mean -0.524). Cross-market with volatility-REACTIVE brackets (target 1.0 sigma / stop 4.0 sigma, sigma = max(ATR14, mean TR of the last 3 bars INCLUDING the event bar)): negative in only 7/12 cells - ZB -0.261/-0.066, ZN -0.239/-0.338 (4/4 negative) but ES +0.003/-0.003, GC +0.018/-0.105, CL -0.137/+0.020, 6E +0.077/+0.098. That is the decisive discriminator: outside the treasuries this is a mis-sized-stop artifact; in ZB/ZN a residual of about -0.24 sigma survives. Scale-free ratio tests (edge_ratio and drift/sigma, p99 vs rest) were only 7/12 and 6/12 in the expected direction across all six markets - i.e. pooled across markets the pure shape statistic shows nothing, and the treasury-specific result rests on the reactive-sigma bracket test plus the fixed-tick lift, not on the ratio test. This is stated as a limitation.
findings.tradeable_form: SUPPRESSION FILTER, not an entry signal. In ZB and ZN: at each 5-min bar close compute |close - prior_close| / ATR14. If it exceeds the trailing 99th percentile (ZB 2.33x ATR14, ZN 2.10x ATR14; both ~6 ticks at median ATR), then for bars k=0,1,2,3 (i.e. the next 20 minutes) place NO new resting limit orders and cancel any unfilled resting limits, on BOTH sides. Resume normal quoting at k=4. This window covers 3.66% of ZB tradable bars and 3.53% of ZN. Existing positions are not touched. Frequency and value on discovery: ZB 691 trigger bars over 351 days (1.97/day, 272 distinct days), of which a depth-1 buy limit would have filled on 571 (p_touch 0.826), saving 0.547 ticks = $17.09 per suppressed fill, $9,761 total; ZN 899 trigger bars over 463 days (1.94/day, 371 distinct days), 767 fills (p_touch 0.853), 0.560 ticks = $8.75 per suppressed fill, $6,713 total. A softer p95 variant (ZB 1.56x ATR14, ZN 1.40x, ~3 ticks) fires on 10/day and saves ZB 0.218t/$6.83 and ZN 0.295t/$4.61 per suppressed fill, $19,396 and $17,346 total - lower per-trade value, more total. NOTE ON THE COST FLOOR: the 0.794-tick (ZB) / 0.938-tick (ZN) floor is the round-trip cost of TAKING a trade. A suppression rule places no order and therefore pays nothing, so its floor is 0 and a 0.541-tick saving clears it. If instead someone tried to turn this into an entry by trading the other way, 0.541 ticks would NOT clear the 0.794-tick floor and it must not be deployed that way. The alternative to suppression, supported by the reactive-sigma result, is to keep quoting but size the bracket to max(ATR14, mean TR of the last 3 bars) - that recovers most of the loss in ES/GC/CL/6E and about a third of it in ZB/ZN.

findings.title: The level of any limit-provision result is NOT identifiable from OHLCV: the touch-vs-through fill assumption is worth ~1.13 ticks, larger than every effect in this dataset - and the incumbent ZB impulse edge is 80% unconditional baseline
findings.observation: Resting a limit order and measuring the outcome from the fill produces a large positive number at EVERY tradable bar in ZB and ZN, with no state required. Unconditional, over all 70,580 tradable ZB discovery bars: a depth-2 buy limit with ttl=6 has p_touch 0.561, drift-from-fill at 12 bars +0.386 ticks, edge_ratio 1.138; a depth-2 sell limit has p_touch 0.567, +0.561 ticks, edge_ratio 1.187. ZN is the same or better (+0.609 / +0.635). With a T3/S12/H48 bracket the unconditional net per fill after commission and slippage is +0.376t (ZB long d2) and +0.521t (ZN long d2). Every one of these numbers reverses sign if the fill rule is tightened by one tick: requiring price to trade THROUGH the limit rather than merely touch it moves ZB d2 from +0.376t to -0.758t and ZN d2 from +0.521t to -0.625t - a swing of 1.13-1.15 ticks, which is larger than any conditional effect measured anywhere in this campaign. Bar data cannot tell us which assumption is right because it contains no queue information. Consequence for the incumbent finding: the reported +0.47 ticks for a depth-2 buy limit after a 24-bar >1.25x ATR up-impulse in calm vol reproduces EXACTLY (+0.4716, p_touch 0.488, and the P(touch) ladder 0.802/0.488/0.266/0.142 matches the brief), but the unconditional baseline for the same instrument, side, depth and geometry is +0.376. The impulse state contributes a LIFT of only +0.095 ticks. At depth 1 the lift is +0.030, at depth 3 +0.142, at depth 4 +0.038; under the through-fill assumption the depth-2 lift falls to +0.060 and the depth-1 lift goes negative (-0.022).
findings.markets: ZB, ZN (measured); the same touch/through gap of roughly one tick applies by construction to ES, GC, CL, 6E and to every limit-entry result the project has produced.
findings.economic_why: There is no counterparty story for the unconditional +0.4 ticks, which is the point. A 5-min bar's LOW is a print that occurred at the bid; assuming a resting buy limit at exactly that price was filled credits you the full bid-ask bounce, which a real passive order at the back of the queue frequently does not receive. Nothing about 'resting a limit at any random moment in ZB earns +0.38 ticks' is economically believable - if it were, it would be the single most crowded trade in the treasury complex. The honest reading is that the measurement contains an unobservable fill-probability term of order one tick and only DIFFERENCES between states, measured under a common fill assumption, are identifiable. The incumbent's +0.47 is therefore mostly that unobservable term, and its genuinely state-attributable part is +0.095 ticks - real (block-clustered t = 3.93) but an eighth of the ZB cost floor.
findings.exit_evidence: The excursion asymmetry cited as the incumbent's mechanism is also mostly unconditional. ZB long, H=24 from the fill, impulse state vs ALL bars: depth1 ER 1.194 vs 1.140, depth2 1.220 vs 1.138, depth3 1.201 vs 1.110, depth4 1.190 vs 1.065. The state adds 0.05-0.13 of edge_ratio, not the whole 1.14-1.22. Separately, edge_ratio for the SELL side unconditionally exceeds the buy side at every depth in both markets (ZB depth2 1.187 vs 1.138; ZN depth2 1.206 vs 1.214), so 'edge_ratio rises with depth' is a property of the instrument and the measurement, not of the impulse state - in the raw baseline it rises with depth on the sell side (1.163/1.187/1.178/1.173 for depths 1-4) and FALLS on the buy side (1.140/1.138/1.110/1.065). Practical exit implication: bracket geometry dominates the reported number far more than the state does. On the same unconditional ZB depth-2 pool, T2/S8/H24 nets +0.352t and T6/S6/H48 nets +0.077t - a 0.28-tick spread from geometry alone, three times the incumbent state's entire lift.
findings.robustness: Reproduction is exact against the numbers in the brief (P(touch) 0.80/0.49/0.27/0.14 at depths 1/2/3/4; net from fill +0.47 at depth 2), which validates the harness. The lift decomposition is computed on the identical event set: 15,391 tradable discovery bars in the impulse state, 7,510 depth-2 fills, 841 de-overlapped episodes at H=48, block-clustered t of the lift = 3.93 (depth 3: t=2.81, depth 1: t=1.59, depth 4: t=2.22). The touch/through gap was measured at depths 1, 2 and 3, both sides, both markets: ZB long 1.061/1.134/1.163 ticks, ZB short 1.028/1.095/1.135, ZN long 0.996/1.146/1.152, ZN short 1.010/1.102/1.165 - consistently ~1.1 ticks. Because the gap is a near-constant level shift, LIFT (state minus unconditional baseline at the same side/depth/geometry) IS stable across the two assumptions: verified directly on the p99 finding above, where the baseline moves 1.08 ticks but the lift moves only 0.045. This is the reason every number in the other finding is reported as a lift.
findings.tradeable_form: This finding removes a trade rather than adding one, and changes the measurement protocol. (1) Do not deploy anything on the strength of an absolute E[net | filled] computed from OHLCV; the number is unidentified to +/-0.55 ticks. Report every limit-entry result as LIFT over the unconditional same-side/same-depth/same-geometry baseline, and check it under BOTH the touch and the trade-through fill rule. (2) The incumbent ZB impulse book should be re-scored on lift: +0.095 ticks at depth 2 against a 0.794-tick floor is REAL BUT UNTRADEABLE, and the position it currently holds in the project's plans is not supported by this measurement. (3) The one cheap way to resolve the ambiguity is empirical, not statistical: the live bot's own resting-limit orders on the demo account already generate the missing data. Log, for every resting limit, whether the bar's extreme merely touched the price or traded through it, and whether the order filled. A few hundred observations pins the fill probability and converts every limit-entry result in the project from a range into a number.

verdicts.title: KILL: the decomposition is exactly right, but the break-even q* is wrong by 1.6-1.9x because eM (+2.43t) exceeds the arithmetic ceiling of their own 2-tick target (+1.856t); corrected q* = 0.77-0.93, and with the exit leg charged the same queue risk the trade is negative in 7 of 8 discovery cells at q=0.5
verdicts.what_i_reproduced:
Wrote my own fill/round-trip engine from scratch (scratchpad/org/v1_decomp.py, v2_roundtrip.py, v3_honest.py, v4_attack.py, v5_final.py), using core.Market only to load bars and the tradable mask.

EXACT REPRODUCTIONS (their arithmetic is sound here):
- n_tradable discovery: ZB 70,580 / ZN 94,464 - exact.
- Snapback (close of fill bar - limit)*side, depth 2 TTL 6: ZB +0.388/+0.431 long/short, ZN +0.538/+0.525 - exact to 3dp.
- Post-fill drift at 12 bars: ZB -0.002/+0.130, ZN +0.072/+0.110 - exact to 3dp.
- Snapback depth curve ZB long at depths 1,2,3,4,6,8,10: 0.357, 0.388, 0.372, 0.354, 0.281, 0.240, 0.145 - exact, digit for digit.
- Through-fill flip: requiring 1 tick beyond the limit takes ZB long snapback to -0.628 and total to -0.671 (they said -0.61/-0.63). The 1.000-tick algebra is right: through-fill at depth d == touch-fill at depth d+1 with a 1-tick-worse entry.
- Exit grid, ZN depth 2 touch-fill, net ticks/fill: t2/s24 +0.4714, t2/s12 +0.4658, t2/s6 +0.4220, t3/s12 +0.4209, t4/s12 +0.2915. They claimed +0.471/+0.466/+0.422/+0.421 and "target 4 lower". Match to 3dp - my simulator and theirs are the same simulator.
- eG (through/certain-fill population, full round trip w/ commission, 0.5t stop slip, 1.0t time slip): ZB -0.750/-0.705, ZN -0.627/-0.623. They claimed "-0.63 to -0.75". Exact.
- nG/nM (event-level): ZB 25,953/13,608, ZN 36,300/19,531. These are the counts their own q* formula implies.
- Outcome mix at t2/s12/mh24: p(target) 0.886, p(stop) 0.024, p(time) 0.090, mean hold 5.19 bars (they said 0.87/0.05/0.08/5.0).
- misalignment_null on the post-fill directional term: ZB short z=2.70, ZN short z=3.01, ZB long z=0.25, ZN long z=1.65. Reproduces their 2.30/3.02/-0.61/1.04 in sign and conclusion - only the short leg beats the null, and only by +0.11 to +0.13 ticks, ~6x below the cost floor. Their own concession is correct.
- random_entry_control 12-bar drift: ZB +0.016, ZN +0.011, CI spans zero in all four cells. Confirms there is no unconditional drift to harvest.
- LOOKAHEAD: I found none material, and I checked the obvious trap. Their exit correctly excludes the fill bar. I measured what same-bar exit would do: eG goes -0.808 -> +0.966 and eM +0.916 -> +1.516, turning everything profitable. They did not take that credit. Fill scan uses bars i+1..i+ttl only; stops win intrabar ties. Clean.
- effective_n does NOT break them. Raw 165,044 is 100% overlapping (every tradable bar is an event), but de-overlapped at the 30-bar window (6 TTL + 24 hold) I get ZB 2,449 episodes / 351 days and ZN 3,266 / 463 - sum 5,715 vs their claimed 6,373, same ballpark. The sequential sim yields 1,300-5,000 genuinely non-overlapping trades per cell. Power is adequate; that is not the failure mode.
- ZB/ZN cross-market agreement is real and close. ES/GC controls are -3.75 and -5.95 ticks, entirely explained by commission in ticks (1.44 and 2.20) - cost-dead, no information.

So the qualitative thesis - the edge is entry price improvement, not prediction; the post-fill directional term is ~zero; the whole thing is a queue-position bet - is CONFIRMED. What fails is the one number the conclusion rests on.
verdicts.what_broke:
Five failures, the first of which is a provable arithmetic error in the load-bearing number.

(1) eM IS ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE - the decisive break. They report eM (kiss-only population) = +2.43 to +2.55 ticks per trade. Their own exit rule is a 2-tick take-profit with commission charged. The maximum attainable net on any such trade is target - commission = 1.856 ticks in ZB and 1.712 in ZN. Time-exits can only close BELOW the target (otherwise the target would have triggered) and stops are negative, so eM <= 1.856 by construction. I verified numerically: max(netM) = 1.8560 in ZB and 1.7120 in ZN, with 95.4% / 97.0% of kiss trades already sitting exactly at that ceiling. Measured eM = +1.545/+1.557 (ZB) and +1.512/+1.508 (ZN). Their eM overstates by 1.57-1.65x. Reverse-engineering confirms this is the sole divergence: q* = -nG*eG/(nM*eM), and their nG, nM and eG all reproduce mine exactly, so their q*=0.589 requires eM=2.43 and nothing else.

(2) CORRECTED q* IS 0.77-0.93, NOT 0.47-0.59. Substituting the measured eM: ZB long 0.926, ZB short 0.870, ZN long 0.771, ZN short 0.789. All four are above 0.5. Their headline "q* = 0.467-0.589, falling to ~0.30-0.35 under sequencing" is wrong in the direction that matters. You would need to be filled on 77-93% of the bars where the market merely kisses your price and turns - which is precisely the population where you are LEAST likely to be at the front of the queue.

(3) SPLIT-HALF FAILS, AND 3 OF 8 CELLS ARE UNACHIEVABLE AT ANY q. Chronological halves (split 2024-11-15): ZB h1 long q*=0.992, ZB h1 short 0.757, ZB h2 long 0.816, ZB h2 short 1.070; ZN h1 long 0.821, ZN h1 short 0.661, ZN h2 long 0.650, ZN h2 short 1.124. Three cells have q* > 1.0 - no fill probability, however generous, makes them profitable. The spread across halves within a single cell is up to 0.47 (ZN short 0.661 -> 1.124), which is not the "genuinely robust plateau" they describe. Validation (0.32-0.60) is better than discovery, as they say, but that makes the discovery instability worse, not better - the best-looking segment is the smallest and last.

(4) THE EXIT LEG IS THE SAME UNMEASURED BET AND THEY DID NOT CHARGE IT. Their entire thesis is that a resting limit's fill is unknowable from OHLCV. The +2-tick take-profit is a resting limit. I re-ran their exact tradeable_form (depth 2, TTL 3, target 2, stop 12, maxhold 24, 11:30-14:30 UTC blocked, one position at a time, sequential non-overlapping) with the same q on BOTH legs. At q=0.5: ZB long -0.200 (h1) / -0.392 (h2), ZB short -0.023 / -0.196, ZN long -0.062 / -0.206, ZN short +0.069 / -0.118. NEGATIVE IN 7 OF 8 DISCOVERY CELLS. They claim +0.312/+0.234/+0.377/+0.046/+0.408/+0.329/+0.311/+0.211 and "positive in 12/12 cells at q=0.5". At q=0.3 both legs: -0.342 to -0.894 across all 8 discovery cells, z from -4.4 to -6.5 - uniformly, significantly negative, not their "6 positive, 5 near zero, 1 negative". Even granting them the optimistic entry-only-q reading, q=0.5 gives -0.075 to +0.330, still well short of their +0.31/+0.41 and negative for ZB long h2. Measured break-even q with both legs honest: ZB ~0.66-0.68, ZN ~0.55-0.58. Only validation survives, and only at q>=0.5.

(5) COST FLOOR - INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY AND NOT CLEARED. The record states effect_ticks 0.45, cost_floor_ticks 0.794, clears_cost TRUE. 0.45 < 0.794. The 0.45 is the q=1 (fill-on-every-touch) net with commission and slippage already charged; what it must still clear is the 0.5-tick ADVERSE_BUFFER, which is exactly the queue/selection risk. Measured q=1 net is +0.343/+0.389 (ZB) and +0.466/+0.452 (ZN) against a 0.5-tick buffer - it does not clear, in any cell. And their own G/M split is the proof the buffer is if anything too small: the certain-fill population loses 0.63-0.75 ticks.

ONE THING WORTH PRESERVING. The snapback is not an "effect" that could pass or fail a null - it is an identity of OHLC bars (close >= low, so conditioning on low <= limit forces E[close - limit] > 0). It is real and it is not yours unless you fill. Their instinct to stop mining this data and go measure q with an instrumented order log is correct, and my numbers support it more strongly than theirs did: with break-even q at 0.55-0.68 both-legs and q* > 1 in three discovery half-cells, this is a coin-flip on a parameter no amount of 5-min OHLCV can resolve. Build the logger as pure instrumentation. Do not deploy it as a trade, and do not expect the "$13-30 per margin-slot-hour at q=0.5" - that figure is negative in discovery once the exit is charged honestly.

verdicts.title: Toxic-window phenomenon REPRODUCES, but the mechanism is falsified, the effect halves out-of-sample, and the proposed rule LOSES total P&L in 4/4 validation cells
verdicts.what_i_reproduced:
Wrote my own fill engine + bracket sim from scratch (scratchpad/org/verify.py, attack.py, attack2.py, attack3.py); did not run their code. Events = all tradable bars, buy/sell limit at depth 2, TTL 6, bracket +2t target / 12t stop / 24-bar time exit, charging commission + 0.5t stop slippage + 1.0t time-exit slippage. 12 cells (ZB,ZN x long,short x disc_h1,disc_h2,validation; discovery split at 2024-08-26).

CONFIRMED: (1) EV(11:30-14:30) - EV(rest) is NEGATIVE in 12/12 cells, mean -0.450t (their claim 0.42t), validation-only -0.398t. Day-clustered bootstrap CI excludes zero in 7/12 (z -0.92 to -4.30). (2) My independent q* (break-even queue-fill prob on the kissed subset) makes 11:30-14:30 the worst of six windows in 11/12 cells; my values 0.42-1.37 vs their 0.58-1.22. (3) MAE12 explodes 1.1-3.5t -> 4.5-7.1t; P(MAE12>=4t) 0.06-0.37 -> 0.43-0.62; edge ratio 1.20-1.76 -> 1.07-1.27. All reproduce. (4) Effective N is fine, NOT hidden overlap: 319-1156 de-overlapped 12-bar episodes and 102-241 distinct days per window-cell. (5) No lookahead — the state is hour-of-day, exogenous. (6) With the full honest floor (adding the 0.5t adverse buffer) the window is net-negative in 12/12 (mean -0.369t) while the rest is +0.081t (negative in only 4/12). (7) Selection null I built myself (500 random 3h window placements): ZB disc_h1 long real -0.019 vs null mean +0.481, z=-2.23, pct 0.032; the window ranks 1st-3rd worst of 48 overlapping 3h windows in 8/12 cells.
verdicts.what_broke:
SIX FAILURES.

1. MECHANISM FALSIFIED (the big one). Matched on realized forward volatility (8 deciles of mean TR over the 12 bars after fill), the disadvantage vanishes and FLIPS: vol-matched EV diff is +0.138t on average, positive in 8/12 cells. Vol-matched edge ratio is HIGHER in the "toxic" window (1.224 vs 1.190, higher in 8/12). Conditional on the same realized volatility a 12:30 fill is at least as good as any other fill. There is no adverse selection here. What the clock actually does is FORECAST a vol expansion that trailing ATR has not yet seen — it is not redundant with trailing ATR (trailing-ATR-matched diff still -0.10 to -0.64 in 12/12; within low-ATR fills only, -0.15 to -0.73 in 12/12, 7/12 CI-clean) — but "informed counterparty takes the other side" is not what the data shows. Correct label: a volatility-timing signal, not a toxicity signal.

2. THE RULE LOSES MONEY IN ABSOLUTE TERMS. skip_clock raises EV/trade in 12/12 but REDUCES total ticks in 9/12 cells and in 4/4 validation cells: ZB valid long 8089->7193, ZB valid short 7564->6668, ZN valid long 10222->9389, ZN valid short 10155->9066 (~11-12% of P&L given away). It only becomes P&L-positive if ADVERSE_BUFFER_TICKS=0.5 is real — and core.py documents that as an unmeasured placeholder. The entire economic case rests on an assumption, not a measurement.

3. VALIDATION DECAY. q* in the window exceeds 1.0 in 3/12 of my cells, ALL in discovery. In all four validation cells q* is 0.42-0.52 — a ~50% queue-fill rate still breaks even there. Validation EV in the window is +0.30 to +0.40t, positive. "Fills there are immediately run over" and "the single largest controllable loss in the book" are not supported out of sample.

4. NULL IS A NON-TEST. Their null_z=0. I ran misalignment_null: z=-0.78, beats_null=False. It cannot possibly test this — a circular WHOLE-DAY outcome shift preserves hour-of-day exactly, so the library null is structurally blind to any clock hypothesis. My proper selection null gives pct=0.032 in one cell, which after Bonferroni over ~8 independent 3h windows is p~0.26, i.e. not significant per-cell; it only earns credibility from the OOS repeat, which is strong in ZN validation (rank 3/48 both sides) but weak in ZB validation (rank 8-9/48).

5. COST ARITHMETIC IS WRONG IN THEIR OWN SUBMISSION. effect_ticks 0.42 vs cost_floor_ticks 0.794, marked clears_cost=true. 0.42 < 0.794. Also a category error: this is a difference between two mostly-positive-EV populations, not a per-trade edge that must clear a floor.

6. RULE IS 3-4x TOO WIDE, AND "DEPTH DOESN'T RESCUE" IS WRONG. Damage concentrates on print-like days (a >3xATR bar in 12:24-13:42), only 19-32% of days: tox EV there is -0.09 to -0.77, but on the other ~70% of days tox EV is +0.14 to +0.65 in 10/12 cells. A blanket every-day 3-hour cancel kills mostly fine trades. And at depth 4 the window is as good as or better than the rest in 3/6 cells I tested (ZB disc_h2 +0.212 vs -0.086; ZN disc_h2 +0.507 vs +0.149; ZB valid +0.281 vs +0.295) — contradicting "depth does not rescue this window". Separately, "12 independent cells" is false: ZB/ZN are the same rate shock and long/short trade the same bars; the real evidence is ~2 periods x 1 market complex.

verdicts.title: KILL: the ZB/ZN deep-limit "give-back" edge is an exact-touch fill artifact plus a second-half-only regime effect; the tradeable form flips to -0.60 t/trade under trade-through fills and the mirror BUY side earns the same as the SELL side
verdicts.what_i_reproduced: I wrote my own touch/fill/outcome code (scripts in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FutureTradingBot/25529eed-cfb9-5eb3-98ab-625b175d900a/scratchpad/org/s1..s7.py) and reproduced the headline closely. verdicts.what_broke:
FIVE independent failures.

(1) FILL REALISM — the decisive one. Their fill rule is high >= limit, i.e. a single touch of the bar's extreme high counts as a fill. Requiring an actual trade-through (high strictly > limit) removes only 26-33% of fills but removes ALL of the edge: ZB D=4 sell d24 +0.851 -> -0.080; ZN D=4 +0.754 -> -0.215; ZN D=6 +0.782 -> -0.133; ZB D=8 +1.657 -> +1.010 (still under its floor); ZN D=8 +1.097 -> +0.323; ZB D=4 edge_ratio 1.134 -> 1.007, ZN D=4 1.121 -> 0.983. The entire "what a fill earns" number lives in the exact-touch subset — precisely the fills a 1-lot retail queue at the extreme of a spike is least likely to receive. This is textbook adverse selection and it is not in their cost buffer, it is in the fill model.

(2) MIRROR SIDE — the claimed directional asymmetry contributes almost nothing to the tradeable form. My one-position-at-a-time sim of their exact recommended config (ZN sell limit D=4, TTL 6, target 4, stop 24, max hold 96, EOD flat, comm + 0.5t adverse + 0.5t stop slip + 1.0t time-exit slip) gives +0.417 t/trade, n=3,052. The identical geometry on the BUY side gives +0.364 t/trade, n=3,024. Nearly the same. The money is the mechanical target-exit-on-a-wick geometry, not "bonds give back fast rallies". ZB D=6/t6/s16: sell +0.283 (t_dayclust=+1.27), buy +0.030 — an asymmetry, but insignificant.

(3) SAME SIM UNDER TRADE-THROUGH FILLS: ZN D=4/t4/s24 goes +0.417 -> -0.602 t/trade (t_dayclust=-3.60, 4/21 months positive, -$20,539). ZB D=6/t6/s16 goes +0.283 -> -0.764 (t=-2.76, 3/17 months). Even with the 0.5t adverse buffer set to zero, both stay negative (-0.102 and -0.264). The recommended trade is a loser, not a marginal winner.

(4) SPLIT-HALF — worse than they admit, and it fails on the FULL quantity too, which they claimed was stable. Calendar-midpoint split of discovery. ZB D=8 sell full_d24: H1 +0.686 / H2 +2.311 (they reported H1 +1.377 / H2 +1.974 — I could not reproduce that stability; their split appears to be by fill count, which pushes the boundary to 2024-11-11 and hides it; with that split I get +1.307/+2.007). H1 +0.686 is less than half the ZB cost floor. ZN D=8 sell full_d24: H1 -0.202 / H2 +2.142 — outright SIGN FLIP in the sibling market. Predictive component ZN D=8: H1 -0.560 / H2 +1.647; ZN D=6: H1 -0.268 / H2 +0.775. Under trade-through fills every ZB and ZN sell cell has a negative H1 (ZB D=4 -0.497, D=6 -0.300, D=8 -0.028; ZN D=4 -0.587, D=6 -0.935, D=8 -1.050). So attack (2) "does it hold in the sibling market" fails: ZN's first half is the opposite sign. Concentration compounds this: for ZB D=8 the top month (2025-04) is 20.4% of all fills and the top 3 months 40.6%.

(5) THE NULL IS ANTI-CONSERVATIVE. Their z=3.51 comes from core's misalignment_null, whose draw-to-draw spread reflects unconditional-drift variation, not the sampling error of a day-clustered conditional estimate. Measured directly: ZB D=8 sell pred24 mu=+1.111, SE_iid=0.198 (t=5.61), null_std=0.325 (z=3.27, matching their 3.51), but day-clustered SE=0.637 -> t=+1.74. ZN D=8: null z=+2.59 vs day-clustered t=+1.17. ZB D=6: z=+2.62 vs t=+1.49. ZN D=6: z=+1.50 vs t=+0.78. The null is roughly 2x too tight; nothing in the predictive component is significant once fills are clustered by day. Day-clustered t on the FULL quantity is +2.48 (ZB D=8) / +1.82 (ZN D=8) — and that quantity dies to fill realism anyway.

COST FLOOR, recomputed touch-conditionally: ZB comm 0.144t + 1.0t market time-exit slip + 0.5t adverse = 1.644t (their 1.64 is right); ZB D=8 full_d24 = +1.657 clears it by 0.013 ticks = $0.41/trade, i.e. zero. ZN floor is 1.788t against +1.097 — short by 0.69t. With a limit target exit the floor drops to 0.644t (ZB) / 0.788t (ZN), which is why the exit grid found positive cells — but that path is the one destroyed by (1) and (3).

LOOKAHEAD: none in state construction. The "state" is literally every tradable bar, and core's descriptors are trailing/shifted; next_eod uses a known schedule, warmup and roll-gap masks are causal. The lookahead is entirely in the fill model (touch = fill at the limit price), which is finding (1).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE AND WORTH KEEPING: after a deep limit fill the fill bar's close sits inside the limit by +0.55t (ZB D=8 sell) / +0.24t (ZB D=8 buy) — the mechanical wick component is itself asymmetric, and it is roughly half of the headline. Their ES "exact mirror" claim also does not survive at matched tick depths: ES buy-limit fills earn +1.575 (d24, D=4) and sell-limit fills lose -0.883, which is just the index's upward drift, not "fast moves extend in both directions".

verdicts.title: KILL — the \"universal +0.4-0.6 tick liquidity-provision constant\" is the bid-ask half-spread; the explorer's martingale control was built without a spread, so it could not detect its own artifact
verdicts.what_i_reproduced:
I rewrote touch_conditional from scratch (/tmp/.../scratchpad/org/v1_repro.py, no import of core.touch_conditional) and reproduced the headline to 3 decimals. ZB (buy+sell)/2 at h=12, ttl=6, depths 1-4: +0.407/+0.473/+0.466/+0.405 (claimed 0.407/0.474/0.466/0.405). ZN: +0.513/+0.622/+0.636/+0.591 (claimed identical). Unconditional 12-bar drift ZB -0.0529t, ZN -0.0229t. p_touch ZB 0.825/0.564/0.370/0.245. The arithmetic is correct.

THEN I measured the h-profile the explorer never reported. The entire quantity is present at h=1 and does not grow: ZB depth2 avg = 0.453 (h=1), 0.468, 0.480, 0.483, 0.473 (h=12), 0.530 (h=48). ZN depth2 = 0.587 (h=1) -> 0.617 (h=48). That is a one-shot offset, not accumulating drift — the signature of a mark-to-print artifact.

DECISIVE CONTROL (v2_bounce.py, v3_matched.py). The explorer's control was a MID-price martingale on the tick grid with NO bid-ask spread — which is exactly why it returned ~0. I rebuilt it two ways from the same driftless random walk: (a) no bounce -> avg12 = -0.010/-0.023/-0.019/-0.010, matching their ~0; (b) same walk plus nothing but a 1-tick bid/ask bounce (Roll), with n_sub/p_move tuned so synthetic p_touch matches real ZB/ZN p_touch to within 0.01-0.03 -> ZB +0.314/+0.384/+0.389/+0.374, ZN +0.416/+0.461/+0.471/+0.466. A series with ZERO predictability reproduces 70-90% of the claim, flat in depth AND flat in horizon, just like the real data.

INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION from a completely different statistic: Roll half-spread from 5-min close-to-close autocovariance = ZB 0.453t, ZN 0.527t, ES 1.140t. The claimed "constant that appears at every depth, every timeframe, both markets" IS the effective half-spread. ES "behaving differently" is just ES having a different half-spread.

RESIDUAL over the bounce null: ZB +0.093/+0.089/+0.077/+0.031, ZN +0.097/+0.162/+0.165/+0.124 — vs cost floors 0.794t (ZB) / 0.938t (ZN). The genuine non-microstructure component is 5-25x below the floor, not the claimed 1.7x.

CORROLLARY (adv_v6.py): the project's INCUMBENT edge is the same artifact. The 24-bar >1.25xATR calm-vol up-impulse state gives buy-limit depth-2 fill->d12 = +0.467t; the identical geometry on EVERY tradable bar with no state at all gives +0.386t. The celebrated state adds +0.08t over doing it at random, and the +0.386 baseline is itself the half-spread.
verdicts.what_broke:
Failed on control mis-specification, mechanism, exit evidence, fill-model robustness, and cost floor. Passed only split-half and precision.

1. NULL (fatal). No null was ever run on the claimed quantity — the record says null_z: 0. Their only control lacked a bid-ask spread, i.e. it controlled away the sole generator of the effect. Against a properly specified Roll-bounce null the effect largely vanishes (residual ZB +0.089, ZN +0.162 at depth 2). core.misalignment_null also fails (ZB z=-1.37, ZN z=-1.09, beats_null False) and random_entry_control gives -0.132t (ZB) / -0.091t (ZN) — but both test unconditional drift and are not the right null here.

2. EXIT EVIDENCE COLLAPSES. They cite edge_ratio 1.187 real vs 1.013 martingale as proof of genuine excursion asymmetry. Against the BOUNCE null: ZB real buy 1.089 / sell 1.143 vs null buy 1.074 / sell 1.156; ZN real 1.142/1.148 vs null 1.117/1.172. The asymmetry is entirely microstructure. Their "the martingale confirms genuine negative short-horizon autocorrelation" is true and trivial — bid-ask bounce IS negative autocorrelation of trade prints, and it is not harvestable.

3. FILL MODEL FLIPS THE SIGN. touch_conditional assumes one print at your price = your fill. In ZB the top of book is deep, so a mere touch fills only the queue front. Requiring trade-through by one tick: ZB avg12 goes +0.407/+0.473/+0.466/+0.405 -> -0.527/-0.534/-0.595/-0.620; ZN +0.513..+0.591 -> -0.378..-0.428. The sign of the effect is set by an unmeasurable queue assumption, not by the data.

4. COST FLOOR, TOUCH-CONDITIONALLY AND SPREAD-HONESTLY. You fill passively at the bid but you are marked against a random bid/ask print, i.e. the mid — the half-spread is booked instantly and cannot be realised, because any exit must cross back. Gross minus the independently-estimated Roll half-spread: ZB -0.047/+0.020/+0.013/-0.048, ZN -0.014/+0.095/+0.109/+0.063 ticks, BEFORE the 0.144t commission and before any adverse-selection buffer.

5. EFFECTIVE N misreported. Claimed n_episodes 2680; I get 1539 (ZB) and 2067 (ZN) at H=48 from 70580/94464 raw — 46x overlap. Precision is not the problem though: day-clustered SEs give ZB buy t=3.33, sell t=5.17; ZN buy t=6.41, sell t=6.74 over 348-461 days. The number is measured precisely. It is just measuring the spread.

6. TRADEABLE-FORM NUMBERS ARE SELECTION. "+0.150 t/trade (t=0.65)" and "+0.288 (t=2.15)" are best-of-63 exit geometries with medians of -0.058 and -0.053. Best-of-63 at t=2.15 is not significant.

7. LOOKAHEAD: none in state construction — the state is "every tradable bar", so there is nothing to leak. Clean on that axis alone. Gap-through fills are handled conservatively. The bias is fill-model optimism, not lookahead.

WHAT SURVIVES: split-half is stable (ZB depth2 H1 +0.493 / H2 +0.455; ZN H1 +0.636 / H2 +0.609), and so is the residual (ZB +0.109/+0.071, ZN +0.176/+0.148). Both markets same sign. But a spread is stable in both halves of any sample — stability here is evidence for the artifact, not against it.

verdicts.what_broke:
Five independent kills.

(1) THE PEAK IS AN ASSUMED CONSTANT, NOT A MEASUREMENT. core.py sets TIME_EXIT_SLIP_TICKS=1.0 and its own comment calls it "a placeholder pending live measurement." At slip=0 the ZB argmax moves 2 -> 4 and the curve is FLAT from T=3 to T=8 (+0.776/+0.781/+0.780/+0.757/+0.760/+0.744 — 0.037t spread over six ticks of target); ZN flattens T3-T5 (+1.037/+1.030/+1.002). At slip=2.0 the argmax pins to T=2 in both. The whole single-peaked shape is generated by how much you charge yourself to flatten. Their text names this mechanism and never varied the knob.

(2) SCALING CLAIM IS BACKWARDS. Their "ZN log-log slope = +0.00" is an artifact of integer argmax over a flat top. Parabolic interpolation on the SAME curves gives monotone T_opt: ZN 2.23/2.41/2.51/2.84/3.81 across medATR 1.14->3.64t (slope +0.459); ZB 2.03/2.11/2.38/2.30/3.23 (slope +0.314). A model-free DiD needing no argmax — [net(T2)-net(T6)]_lowVol minus _highVol — is POSITIVE in all five markets: ZB +0.493, ZN +0.531, ZF +0.672, ZT +0.334, 6E +0.477 ticks (and still positive at slip=0). The optimum unambiguously shifts right as vol rises.

The numbers survive; the interpretation and the prescription do not. Five failures:
(1) SESSION CONFOUND kills the low-end monotonicity. The calm bucket is 86% Asia (ZB) / 78% (ZN); the wild bucket is 69% / 73% US. Their robustness claim "monotone across all 8 buckets in both markets with no inversions" is true only in the pooled sample. Variance decomposition: hour-of-day explains MORE forward-range variance than atr_pct (R2 0.254 vs 0.198 ZB; 0.253 vs 0.166 ZN), so "atr_pct is a clean causal predictor of the next 2 hours' range" overstates a predictor the clock beats.
(2) TOUCH-CONDITIONAL INVERTS THE HEADLINE. This is the decisive attack and the project's own mandated measurement. Drift-from-fill at 12 bars is FLAT, not worse in calm: ZB 0.52 (calm) vs 0.40 (wild); ZN 0.42 vs 0.57. This holds in both chronological halves (ZB h1 1.256->1.123, h2 1.234->1.093; ZN h1 1.207->1.141, h2 1.244->1.101), WITHIN the US session alone so it is not the clock (ZB 1.375->1.103; ZN 1.275->1.109), and under ATR-scaled depth at 0.5x and 1.0x ATR so it is not a fixed-depth artifact (ZB 1.269->1.108; ZN 1.272->1.127). Honest caveat that partly defends them: absolute MFE-MAE in ticks mildly favours loud (ZB 0.79 calm vs 0.98 wild; ZN 0.87 vs 1.21), and nothing clears the floor (drift-from-fill 0.39-0.53t vs 0.794t). The correct statement is "roughly FLAT across vol buckets", not "calm is worst".
(3) DIRECTIONAL NULL NOT REPRODUCIBLE. They cite bar-shuffle z=-2.03/-2.02 (ZB). What is actually stable is the median attainable move in TICKS (2.5-3.0 across the bottom four buckets), not the multiplier.

verdicts.what_broke:
NULL (primary, fatal). Their misalignment_null passes (I ran it: ZN mom6 fade side real=+0.211, null_mean=0.000, z=+2.43, beats_null=True) but it is the WRONG null for this claim. It randomizes event TIMING while holding the trade side fixed, so it structurally cannot detect an effect that comes from conditioning the side on the bar's own direction. Against the correct baseline — all bars signed by their own sign(C-O) — the excess is zero. Their z=-3.13 measures "bars drift against their own direction", which is true of all 61,428 ZN bars, not of extremes.
Also, ZB vol8x fails even their own null one-sided: up-events z=+2.19 (real +0.599), down-events z=-0.34 (real -0.080, beats_null=False). A real inventory-unwind effect would be symmetric.

SPLIT-HALF. Signs mostly agree but sizes are unstable and nearly every half-sample is insignificant. ZB vol8x 12-bar: H1 -0.133 (t=-0.46) vs H2 -0.384 (t=-1.63). ZB mom24 24-bar SIGN FLIPS: H1 -0.359 vs H2 +0.003. ZN vol4x 24-bar SIGN FLIPS: H1 +0.055 vs H2 -0.269. ZN vol8x 24-bar SIGN FLIPS: H1 +0.126 vs H2 -0.376. Only the drought (the pure microstructure artifact) is stable in both halves — which is exactly what an artifact should do.

And it is not event-specific: an ALL-BARS no-event limit at depth 2 gives ZN +0.585 (edge_ratio 1.132), and a fade-side limit at ALL bars gives ZN +0.721 (edge_ratio 1.144). The event conditioning makes the touch-conditional outcome WORSE than doing it at random bars. ZB: event ZB_vol8x depth 2 gives +0.808 vs ZB all-bars +0.427 — the only place event conditioning helps, but this is the incumbent liquidity-provision effect in a high-volume state, not the fade, and its misalignment null fails on the short side.

verdicts.what_i_reproduced: I wrote my own fill/bracket engine (adv_clock/vlib2.py; only core.Market used for bar loading, none of core.py's measurement functions) and reproduced the claimed table to 3 decimals. verdicts.what_broke:
(1) SPLIT-HALF — the clock is anti-persistent. Chronological half-split of discovery (ZB at 2024-09-30, ZN at 2024-07-15): correlation of the 23-hour value profile between halves is ZB spearman -0.170 / pearson -0.128, ZN spearman +0.170 / pearson +0.115 — i.e. zero. Honest out-of-sample hour selection (rank hours on H1, trade them on H2): ZB in-sample spread +0.494 t collapses to OUT-OF-SAMPLE -0.137 t; ZN +0.404 -> -0.062 t; reversing the direction gives -0.060 (ZB) and +0.056 (ZN); selecting on ZB-H1 and testing on ZN-H2 gives -0.114. All five selections lose relative to the 'bad' hours. The claim's good/bad sets (03,04,11,18,22 vs 00,02,10,12,15) show a spread in both halves (ZB +0.306/+0.371, ZN +0.138/+0.183) only because those sets were chosen with full-sample knowledge; the researcher's own list of 'UNSTABLE cells' is the visible tip of that selection. Coarse session blocks (no cherry-picking) kill it: ZN block spread is only 0.119 t with block-profile H1-vs-H2 correlation -0.658; ZB spread 0.236 t.
(2) THE WRONG NULL WAS USED. A bar-shuffle null destroys short-horizon mean reversion, so its expected touch-conditional value is ~0 at every hour; it tests 'is provision value positive', not 'is hour 22 special'. The correct null — permute hour labels WITHIN each day, 400 draws, statistic = max-min across hours — gives ZB observed 0.652 t vs null mean 0.515, p95 0.715, z=1.18, p=0.142; ZN observed 0.479 t vs null mean 0.428, p95 0.612, z=0.50, p=0.250. NEITHER MARKET BEATS THE NULL. Hours deviating from the pooled mean at |cluster-t|>2: ZB 2/23, ZN 0/23 (chance ~1.2/23). core.py's own misalignment_null returns beats_null=False on every flagship state (ZN h04 z=0.11, ZN h22 z=0.37, ZB h04 z=0.64, ZB h22 z=-0.18); random_entry_control gives -0.03 to -0.30 ticks.
(3) LEVEL REPORTED AS EFFECT. effect_ticks=0.722 is the LEVEL at one hour, not the hour effect. All 23 hours are positive; pooled fill-weighted value is +0.474 t (ZB) and +0.622 t (ZN). The real hour excess is 0.722-0.622 = +0.10 t in ZN; the good-minus-pooled contrast is +0.039 t (ZN) and +0.164 t (ZB). The claimed 'factor of 6' is 2.0x in ZN and in ZB is carried by the single hour 00.
(4) COST FLOOR, TOUCH-CONDITIONALLY. Instead of the notional 0.5-tick adverse buffer I measured penetration directly. Requiring the tape to trade 1 tick THROUGH the limit turns EVERY hour in BOTH markets negative: ZB pooled -0.529 t, ZN pooled -0.343 t; best cells ZN h04 -0.005, ZB h22 -0.269. Blending by q (fill prob on a pen=0 touch): ZN h04 net of commission + stop slip + time-exit slip is +0.519 t at q=1.0, +0.259 at q=0.5, +0.019 at q=0.25, -0.412 at q=0. Pooled over all hours it is already negative at q=0.5 (ZN -0.206, ZB -0.268). The implied value of a pen=0 fill is +1.70 to +2.77 ticks against a 2-tick target — a tautology, since 'the low equalled my limit and never went below' is by construction a bounce whose stop cannot be hit. Those are exactly the fills a back-of-queue order does not get. Worse, the edge is largest where q is smallest: at ZB h04 median 5-min range is 1 tick, 86% of bars have range<=1 tick, median 5-min volume is 107 contracts (ZN h04: 462). Their '+0.716 net of commission' is gross minus commission with the adverse-selection buffer silently dropped (floor 0.938 conceded but then not applied).
(5) EFFECTIVE N. ZN h04: 2852 raw fills de-overlap to 354 at H=24 — 8.1 fills/day inside a 1-hour bucket, ~8x overlap. Their episode count is honest but their t is not (cluster-by-day 12.88, not 15.0), and 354 episodes is one cell out of 23 hours x 2 markets x several depths, so z=2.64 survives no selection correction.
(6) CONSTRUCTION BUG on the evening hours. forward_matrix indexes by BAR not by clock, so the +24-bar window jumps the Globex close. Share of events whose window spans >120 min of wall clock: ZB h20 = 0.898 (median span 180 min), h19 = 0.640, h22 = 0.432; ZN h20 = 0.885, h19 = 0.600. Hour 20 is ZN's single best cell (0.950) and ZB's second best (0.659) — both are measuring the overnight reopen, not the hour.
