Since the unconditional limit is already ~0.3 ticks short of the floor, a +0.2-0.3 tick shape bonus does not close the gap.

ES HAS NO CONDITIONAL STRUCTURE AT LIMIT FILLS — IT IS ALL BETA. ES unconditional 24-bar drift over discovery is +1.0365 ticks. Buy-limit fills at depth 6 give a 24-bar predictive drift of +1.430 (excess only +0.39) and sell-limit fills -1.196 (excess only -0.16). p_touch at 1-4 ticks is 0.79-0.96 because a 5-min ES bar spans ~24 ticks, so tick-denominated depths are meaningless there; ATR-scaled depths show clean momentum but nothing above the +2.09 tick cost floor. ES is cost-dead for this family of behaviours.

THE INCUMBENT ZB FINDING IS ~85% UNCONDITIONAL. The all-bar ZB baseline for a buy limit 2 ticks below the close (TTL 6) is d12 = +0.386 ticks, d24 = +0.343, p_touch 0.560, edge_ratio 1.138, on 39,561 fills. The incumbent's +0.47 after a 24-bar up-impulse in calm volatility is therefore only about +0.08 ticks better than doing it at a randomly chosen bar. The reported p_touch ladder (0.80/0.49/0.27/0.14 at depths 1-4) is also close to the unconditional ladder (0.82/0.56/0.37/0.24). The incumbent state is not adding much; the limit order is doing the work.

MEASURED-AND-DISCARDED: ranked the top 40 words at k=2,3,4 in ZB and ZN by occurrence and ran touch-conditional at depths 1-4 on both sides (1,437 cells with >=150 fills). The largest excesses over baseline reached +1.68 ticks (ZB k=3 'iei' buy depth 3, 178 fills) and the largest negatives -1.37. Both tails are what a 1,437-cell scan produces by chance at those fill counts; none survived the split-half test above. Reported here so nobody re-mines it.

POST-FILL DRIFT IN ZB AND ZN IS ZERO. This is the most important negative result and it kills the directional interpretation of the incumbent edge. Measured as (C[fill_bar+h] − C[fill_bar])×side, which is completely independent of any fill-price assumption. Over 48 bars at depth 2/4/6/8/10 the numbers are: ZB long disc_h1 +0.09/+0.07/+0.16/+0.20/+0.19 but disc_h2 −0.34/−0.79/−1.18/−1.56/−1.84 and validation +0.26/+0.48/+1.01/+1.36/+1.22. Sign flips between the two halves of discovery and flips back in validation. De-overlapped episode z-scores are |z| < 1.2 in every discovery cell. Same picture in ZN. Conclusion: after a limit fills in ZB or ZN, the market does nothing for you. Any depth-dependent drift you see is the prevailing rate regime, not spike reversion.

THE 'DEEP SHORT-SIDE SPIKE REVERSION' IN ZB IS A REGIME ARTIFACT. Selling a limit 14 ticks above the close and holding shows +2.97 ticks at 12 bars and +2.36 at 48 in pooled discovery, with a monotone ramp in depth (post-48 drift 0.24/0.39/0.53/0.65/1.10/1.69/2.12/2.47/2.36 at depths 1–14) — the most seductive-looking curve in the whole study. It is dead: disc_h1 gives +0.02 to +1.01, disc_h2 gives +0.58 to +2.82, validation gives −0.17 to −2.19. The sign reverses in validation, de-overlapped episode |z| < 1.7 everywhere, and only 65–360 independent episodes exist at depths 8–10. It is 'bonds fell on volatile days in late 2024 and rose on volatile days in late 2025', nothing more.

STATE CONDITIONING ADDS NOTHING TO THE TOUCHCURVE. I swept 20 entry states (24-bar impulses at 1.25/2.0/3.5/5.0 ATR up and down, 6-bar impulses at 2.0 ATR, range compression at rng12 < 2.0/2.5 ATR, single bars with range > 1.6/2.0 ATR split by direction, high-vol, calm, unconditional) × 2 sides × 14 depths × 4 TTLs = 5,376 cells for ZB and ZN. I reproduced the incumbent finding exactly (ZB, 24-bar up-impulse > 1.25 ATR in calm vol, buy limit 2 ticks below, TTL 6: p_touch 0.802/0.488/0.266/0.142 at depths 1–4, 12-bar drift from the fill +0.467 at depth 2). But the impulse filter contributes nothing: the plain 'calm volatility' state alone gives +0.47 at the same depth, and unconditional gives +0.39. The impulse is a proxy for narrow bars, and narrow bars are just where a 2-tick limit is a big excursion. None of the 20 states produced a q* materially below the unconditional case.

SNAPBACK ALONE DOES NOT CLEAR THE HONEST COST FLOOR. The best price improvement available anywhere, under the most optimistic possible fill assumption, is +0.538 ticks (ZN, depth 2, long) and +0.431 (ZB, depth 2, short). The core cost floor at stop_rate 0.3 is 0.794 ticks in ZB and 0.938 in ZN. So if you charge the full 0.5-tick adverse-selection buffer as a cost AND assume you always fill on the touch, the trade is dead. It only lives because the adverse-selection buffer and the fill assumption are the same parameter counted twice — which is exactly why I replaced both with the explicit q* framework rather than dressing up a number.

ES AND GC LIMIT FILLS ARE PURE TREND EXPOSURE, NOT LIQUIDITY PROVISION. Run as controls: ES post-fill 48-bar drift is +0.91 to +0.97 on the long side and −1.98 to −2.63 on the short side in discovery, widening to +1.8/−5.2 in validation; GC is +4.6/−4.8 in discovery and +10.3/−9.9 in validation. Perfectly antisymmetric and growing with sample recency — that is the 2024–25 equity and gold bull markets showing up in the fill statistics, nothing about fill quality. Useful as a sanity check that the decomposition detects drift when drift is present, and that ZB/ZN genuinely have none.

TWO-SIDED QUOTING FROM A SINGLE MARGIN SLOT DESTROYS ROUGHLY TWO THIRDS OF THE EDGE. Measured directly: ZB depth 3, TTL 6, q=0.3, 11:30–14:30 excluded — long-only slot +0.336 ticks/trade (z 4.25), short-only slot +0.347 (z 5.10), but a single slot quoting both sides and taking whichever fills first gives +0.092 (z 1.29). Identical pattern in ZN (+0.444 / +0.417 / +0.233) and at q=0.0 and q=0.5. The mechanism is that a two-sided quote is always filled on the leg the market ran into, and blocks the slot from taking the far better entry available after the run exhausts itself. If you have 4 slots, give each one a single instrument and a single side.

PER-BAR EVENT STUDIES MATERIALLY OVERSTATE THE COST OF LIMIT PROVISION, WHICH IS WHY THE HEADLINE q* DEPENDS ON THE SIMULATION MODE. The per-bar view (quote at every bar, count every fill) gives q* = 0.47–0.59; the deployable one-position-at-a-time view with only the entry leg subject to q gives q* = 0.05–0.16; with both legs subject to q it gives 0.30–0.35. The gap is real and mechanical: in a sustained adverse move every single bar triggers a fill in the event study, so one bad move is counted 5–10 times, whereas a margin-constrained bot takes it once and is then busy. Report the both-legs sequential number (0.30–0.35) as the honest figure. I flag this as a methodological trap the project should not fall into again.

DESTINATIONS ARE A NULL RESULT — price does not seek structural levels in ZB/ZN at 5-min resolution. I built a distance-matched baseline (unconditional P(MFE >= d ticks within 48 EOD-capped bars), computed separately in 5 ATR buckets) and compared every structural destination's actual hit rate against what its distance alone predicts. Over 32 tests across both markets: prior day high (lift +0.006 ZB / +0.003 ZN), prior day low (+0.003 / -0.003), prior close (+0.006 / -0.000), day open (+0.006 / -0.002), running day high (+0.010 / +0.016), running day low (+0.016 / +0.007). Largest |lift| anywhere was 0.042 (ZN prior-day-low approached from below, z=-2.47 — and NEGATIVE, i.e. hit LESS than distance predicts); largest positive z was +2.09 (ZN running day high). With 32 tests those are exactly what noise produces. Round numbers are equally dead at three scales: whole point (+0.005/-0.003 ZB, +0.004/-0.003 ZN), half point (-0.000/+0.001, +0.000/+0.002), quarter point (+0.001/+0.005, +0.009/+0.004). CONCLUSION: destination_hits() adds nothing over a distance model in these contracts. Do not spend further compute on level-seeking, magnet, or liquidity-sweep hypotheses in ZB/ZN — the entire signal in a hit rate is 'how far away was it'.

THE 0.5 GAMBLER'S-RUIN BENCHMARK FOR ROUND-TRIP IS INVALID AND I NEARLY REPORTED A FALSE FINDING FROM IT. Measuring P(reach +2u before returning to entry | touched +u), the raw numbers look like overwhelming mean reversion: 0.363 (ZB) and 0.323 (ZN) at u=2 against an apparent continuous-time fair value of 0.500. But running the identical code on bar-shuffled paths — same bars, same intrabar ranges, same censoring, random order — gives 0.394 and 0.366. So roughly 75-85% of the apparent 'round-trip dominance' is a pure artefact of bar discretisation and horizon censoring, and the true path-dependent component is only -0.027 to -0.041. Any analysis in this project that benchmarks a first-passage race against 0.5 is wrong. Answering the brief's question (d) directly: price does NOT round-trip meaningfully more than its own reshuffled bars at 2-3 ticks, and at 5+ ticks it round-trips LESS.

NO DIRECTIONAL EDGE EXISTS AT ALL — confirmed independently of the incumbent finding. Entering at the event bar's CLOSE (market entry) with the same T/S bracket and assuming ZERO entry slippage, which is deliberately optimistic and impossible: ZB net +0.160t all-bars / +0.147t QUIET; ZN net -0.037t / -0.013t. Charging the realistic 1.0 tick market-entry slip puts these at -0.84t (ZB) and -1.04t (ZN). The entire measured edge in this campaign is the 2-tick price improvement on the limit fill, exactly as the incumbent finding states. Nothing in the destination geometry changes this.

NO HAZARD COLLAPSE — the brief's question (a) has a negative answer in its literal form. P(MFE >= d+1 | MFE >= d) is essentially flat at 0.8956, 0.8815, 0.8729, 0.8693, 0.8669, 0.8671, 0.8667, 0.8655 for d=1..8 in ZB, stays in 0.865-0.872 through d=13, and then RISES to 0.8942 at d=20. ZN is near-identical (0.8936 at d=1, 0.8609 minimum at d=5, 0.8912 at d=20). There is no distance at which the marginal probability of going further collapses. The 2-3 tick optimum of Finding 1 is a net-P&L optimum produced by the cost of the losing tail, not by any change in how price travels.

SEVEN OF NINE OTHER AFFORDABLE MARKETS ARE COST-DEAD FOR THIS GEOMETRY, and the reason is commission measured in ticks, not anything about their behaviour. Running the identical QUIET-state limit-provision measurement with the OPTIMISTIC touch-fill model (which flatters everything) on DISCOVERY data: ES -0.984t (comm 1.440t/trade, f*=2.30), GC -2.591t (comm 2.200t, f*=4.92), CL -1.868t (comm 2.200t, f*=4.03), 6E -1.221t (comm 1.280t, f*=4.26), YM -4.792t (comm 3.600t, f*=9.04), RTY -4.273t (comm 3.600t, f*=9.05), HG -2.258t (comm 2.080t, f*=4.57), ZC -0.136t (comm 0.320t, f*=1.23). An f* above 1.0 is arithmetically unachievable — you cannot fill more than 100% of touched limits. Only three markets besides ZB/ZN are even positive: ZF +0.209t (comm 0.576t, f*=0.703) and ZT +0.030t (comm 0.288t, f*=0.872, and only 3663 fills from 900 episodes because P(touch)=0.146). Neither clears a plausible fill rate. The ranking is a near-perfect inverse of commission-in-ticks, which confirms the brief's cost ordering empirically: ZB (0.144t) > ZN/ZT (0.288t) > ZF (0.576t) >> everything else.

THE SELL SIDE FAILS THE MISALIGNMENT NULL IN BOTH MARKETS. ZB QUIET sell-limit-above: real +0.436t vs day-shifted null mean +0.426t, sd 0.080, z=+0.12, does not beat the null p95 of +0.564. ZN QUIET sell: real +0.515t vs null +0.456t, sd 0.088, z=+0.67, p95 +0.628, fails. Only the buy side survives (ZB z=+1.91, ZN z=+2.49). f* is also far worse on the sell side (ZB 0.503 vs 0.308; ZN 0.399 vs 0.086). I do not have an economic story for a persistent long-side asymmetry in two Treasury contracts over a 2-year sample and I do not believe one should be assumed — this may simply be the 2023-2025 rate path. Treat the buy-only restriction as a robustness precaution, not as a discovered asymmetry, and re-check it if the sample is extended.

ZB IS NOT TEMPORALLY STABLE AND SHOULD BE DEPRIORITISED BEHIND ZN despite its better commission ratio. ZB QUIET buy split-half under the touch model: disc-H1 +0.762t, disc-H2 +0.405t, VALIDATION +0.675t — but the break-even fill rate f* swings 0.117 / 0.497 / 0.218 across those three blocks, meaning in the second half of discovery you would have needed to fill half of all merely-touched limits just to break even. ZN's f* over the same three blocks is 0.080 / 0.092 / 0.160, a factor of two rather than a factor of four. ZB's other warning signs: its state scan produced a spurious day-of-week peak (Thursday +0.679t vs Friday +0.281t) that does not replicate in ZN, and its 'close near day LOW' cell reads +0.098t versus ZN's +0.511t. ZB's raw numbers are noisier at every level.

THE LIBRARY'S ADVERSE_BUFFER OF 0.5 TICKS IS TOO SMALL BY ROUGHLY A FACTOR OF TWO. Measured directly as the gap between the optimistic touch-fill and the pessimistic trade-through-by-1-tick fill on the identical policy and identical state: ZB all-bars 1.050t, ZB QUIET 1.049t, ZN all-bars 1.131t, ZN QUIET 0.954t. So the true touch-vs-through adverse-selection cost is 0.95-1.13 ticks, not 0.50. This is not a reason to raise the constant — a flat tick haircut is the wrong model, because the correct quantity (what fraction of merely-touched limits actually fill) depends on queue depth, which itself correlates with the QUIET state that defines the edge. I recommend the f* decomposition in Finding 3 replace ADVERSE_BUFFER for any limit-entry evaluation in this project.

THE NO-STOP POLICY IS NOT DEPLOYABLE ON THIS ACCOUNT even though it maximises expectancy. ZB T=2 no-stop, EOD-capped: p5=-9.14t, p1=-24.14t, p0.1=-55.59t, worst -87.14t = -$2,723 on a ~$4,100 account, i.e. a single trade can take two-thirds of the account. ZN is milder at worst -83.29t = -$1,301 but with 4-5 concurrent positions a correlated day still threatens the account. Every previous line of this analysis that reads 'stops cost money' must be read alongside this: the S=24 stop costs 0.006-0.016 ticks of expectancy and is mandatory.

SEVERAL PLAUSIBLE CONDITIONING AXES MEASURED FLAT OR INCONSISTENT AND SHOULD NOT BE PURSUED. Trend alignment: ZB trend_up +0.494t vs trend_dn +0.330t looked promising but ZN shows +0.518 vs +0.542 — no effect, and inside the ZN QUIET cell it is +0.815 vs +0.807. Position in the day's range: all four buckets within 0.383-0.538 (ZB) and 0.495-0.568 (ZN) — flat. Prior k-bar impulse magnitude at k=3,6,12,24 signed relative to the limit side: the full range across all 20 impulse cells is 0.215-0.465 (ZB) and 0.447-0.607 (ZN), with no monotone structure and no cross-market agreement on which end is better. Day of week: ZB's best is Thursday (+0.679) and ZN's is Tuesday (+0.608); the only weakly shared feature is Friday being worst in both (+0.281 / +0.400), which is not enough to act on. Proximity to the day's extremes: ZB reads +0.098t near the day low while ZN reads +0.511t — opposite conclusions, discard.

INCUMBENT EDGE IS ZERO ONCE CONTROLLED. Reproduced the ZB incumbent exactly: 24-bar up-impulse >1.25xATR in calm vol, buy limit 2 ticks below close, n_raw 15,391, 898 episodes, 306 days -> +0.467 ticks at 12 bars from the fill (the reported +0.47). But a matched-random control drawn from the SAME session x vol-regime strata gives +0.474. Excess = -0.007 ticks, z = -0.04. Its edge_ratio is also WORSE than control (1.143 vs 1.175). The state contributes literally nothing; 100% of the number is the mechanical touch-conditioning artifact. The correct baseline for any touch-conditional claim is the touch-conditional number at matched random times, not zero and not the unconditional drift. At random times in ZB a 2-tick buy limit already gives +0.386 t and a 2-tick SELL limit gives +0.561 t.

ALL FOUR INVERSIONS OF 'BUY PULLBACKS IN CALM VOL' ALSO NOTHING (ZB, depth 2, excess over matched control, 12-bar): invert direction (sell rally after up-impulse) +0.094 z+0.51; invert vol regime (buy dip in hot vol) +0.007 z+0.02; mirror (sell rally after down-impulse) -0.100 z-0.57; invert direction after down-impulse (buy dip) -0.002 z-0.01. At depth 3-4 the fade-the-impulse versions reach +0.21 to +0.34 with z 0.6-0.8, still nothing. Misalignment null run on all five variants in BOTH ZB and ZN: beats_null=False for every one, |z| <= 1.47. The strongest inverse in the whole set (ZN 'UPimp hot LONG', real -0.186, z -1.47) is a coin flip.

SYSTEMATIC 2-AXIS SCAN FINDS NOTHING IN BONDS. 4 markets x ~22 conditioning cells (impulse-z24 sextiles, 8 UTC hour blocks, 5 vol quintiles, 5 days of week, 4 intraday-position quartiles) x 2 sides = ~176 touch-conditional-excess measurements at depth 3. In ZB the largest |z| is 2.04 (EU session short, excess +0.761); in ZN the largest is 1.47. With 176 tests those are expected under the null. GC produces |z| up to 4.95 (calm-vol long-minus-short gap -4.73 t) but that is entirely gold's 2023-2025 bull trend, not timing: the same gap in hot vol is +0.24 (z+0.13), and the long leg (+2.29 t) still does not clear GC's 2.85 t floor.

UNCONDITIONAL LONG/SHORT LIMIT GAP IN ZB DOES NOT REPLICATE. In discovery, ZB resting SELL limits beat resting BUY limits and the gap grows with depth: +0.126 (d1), +0.175 (d2), +0.274 (d3), +0.427 (d4, z+1.64), +0.745 (d6, z+1.83); edge_ratio short rises 1.118->1.189 while long falls 1.088->0.981. It survives split-halves weakly (H1 +0.175, H2 +0.362 at d3). In VALIDATION it is dead: gap -0.063 (d2), +0.027 (d3), +0.003 (d4), all |z| < 0.4. ZN discovery gap is smaller (+0.026 to +0.173, all z<1) and validation is -0.092/+0.041/+0.133. Do not build on this.

NO UP/DOWN SPEED ASYMMETRY IN BONDS, AND THE APPARENT ONE IN ES/GC IS A DRIFT ARTIFACT. ZB: P(reach +k before -k) vs P(reach -k before +k) = 0.4887/0.4776 at 2t, 0.4979/0.4871 at 3t, 0.4864/0.4709 at 4t, 0.4196/0.4038 at 6t, 0.2049/0.1964 at 12t -- differences <=0.016 with n=70,580. Median bars-to-reach identical to the bar (3/3, 7/7, 10/10, 16/16, 19/19, 24/23). ZN the same. In ES/GC the excursion_stats 'bars_to_mfe' differs (long 25-26 vs short 19-21) but the direct measurement shows median bars-to-first-touch of +/-1.5xATR is 8 up vs 7 down (ES) and 7/7 (GC): the bars_to_mfe difference is caused by drift pushing a long's maximum to the end of the window, not by down-moves being faster. Do not use bars_to_mfe as a speed statistic in a drifting market.

CEILING PROOF: NO MARKET/STOP-ENTRY DIRECTIONAL STRATEGY CAN WORK ON 5-MIN ZB/ZN. Scanned 9 causal features (impulse-z over 6/12/24/96 bars, position-in-day, ATR percentile, volume vs trailing median, close-location-in-range, distance from prior close) x 6 buckets each x 4 horizons = 208 cells in ZB and 212 in ZN. MAXIMUM absolute conditional drift over every cell and horizon: ZB 1.124 ticks, ZN 1.211 ticks -- both at the 48-bar horizon, and both BELOW the market-entry cost floor of 1.794 (ZB) and 1.938 (ZN) ticks. Those maxima are themselves the selection maximum of 200+ cells, so the honest expected value is much lower. Any bot design that enters ZB/ZN with a stop or market order on a 5-minute signal is arithmetically dead before it starts.

EVERY ATR-SCALED BRACKET LOSES IN EVERY MARKET, BOTH SIDES, BOTH SPLITS. Limit entry at depth 2 with the through-fill rule, targets/stops at 1x/1.5x/2x ATR and 1x/3x and 3x/1x ATR, 96-bar cap. Net ticks range: ZB -0.59 to -1.20, ZN -0.59 to -1.20, ES -1.69 to -2.94, GC -2.07 to -5.31. 80 cells, zero positive, z from -1.34 to -29.7. Same-bar target/stop ambiguity is 0.1-2.7% of fills so the conservative 'stop wins ties' rule is not responsible. ES and GC show SHORT strictly worse than LONG in all 20 cells (S-L -0.33 to -1.78) -- the 2023-2025 equity/gold bull trend, present in validation too, but useless because the long leg loses 1.7-3.6 ticks.

THROUGH-FILL STATE SCAN: 60+ CELLS, NOT ONE POSITIVE. In ZB and ZN, guaranteed-fill bracket net measured across: the incumbent state and all three of its inversions, all three sessions, calm/hot, ATR percentile <0.2 and >0.8, all five days of week, at-day-low and at-day-high, quiet vs active 6-bar tape, below-median volume and >2x volume spike, limit depths 1/2/3/4/6/8, and bracket shapes T2S10 through T12S12. Range -0.106 to -1.507 ticks, z from -0.14 to -13.54. The single best cell in the entire scan (ZB calm, depth 8, T6/S18, long: -0.106 +/- 0.744, n=486, 126 days) is UNDERPOWERED by the project's own rule and still negative. There is no state in ZB or ZN where being the passive side of a trade you are certain to get filled on is profitable.

ZB IS WORSE THAN ZN FOR LIQUIDITY PROVISION DESPITE THE LOWER TICK COST FLOOR. ZB's break-even queue fill rate is 0.43-0.44 versus ZN's 0.31-0.36, and ZB's guaranteed-fill loss is larger in dollars (-0.830 t = -$25.9 vs ZN -0.705 t = -$11.0). The 'ZB is best by cost' ranking in the brief is true in commission-per-ATR-tick terms but reverses once adverse selection is priced. If any passive book is deployed, ZN should be the first market, not ZB.

POST-FAILURE DIRECTION IS NOTHING. After a 1xATR adverse excursion, the 12-bar drift measured in the direction the move was travelling is +0.554, +0.188, +0.122, +0.065 (ZB down-failures, speeds 1-2/3-5/6-11/12-23) and -0.046, +0.364, -0.258, -0.114 (ZB up-failures), i.e. the sign flips between the two mirror directions in three of four buckets. Misalignment null (circular whole-day outcome shift, 300 draws) over 16 ZB/ZN cells: only 2 exceed |z|=2 and they point OPPOSITE ways (ZB down-fail spike z=+2.01 continuation, ZN up-fail spike z=-2.23 reversion). With 16 tests you expect ~0.8 such cells by chance. Verdict: price after a failure neither continues nor reverts in any measurable way, at any failure speed, in either market.

THE REVERSAL TRADE IS DEAD ON ARRIVAL. Market-entry brackets taken at the failure bar close, in the direction opposite to the failed position, over 32 cells (ZB+ZN x 2 directions x 4 speed buckets x 4 geometries tp4/sl4, tp6/sl6, tp8/sl8, tp6/sl12, H=48, ties given to the stop, stop charged 0.5 tick of slippage): GROSS mean per trade ranges from -1.140 to +0.202 ticks, with 28 of 32 negative. Against the honest market-entry cost floor of 1.794t (ZB) / 1.938t (ZN), NET is between -1.649 and -2.934 ticks in every single cell. Not one positive. The mission's question 'is the post-failure move large enough to trade in the opposite direction after costs' has a flat answer: no, and it is not close -- the gross edge is zero, so the entire cost is a dead loss.

THE SNAPBACK IS AN ILLUSION OF DISTANCE. P(price returns to the original reference price within 48 bars) looks dramatic and is perfectly monotone in failure speed: ZB down-failures 0.864 (spike) / 0.826 / 0.760 / 0.586 (grind); ZN 0.891 / 0.802 / 0.723 / 0.603; same for up-failures. But a matched-random control -- random tradable bars, the SAME distribution of normalized distance (dist/ATR), same 48-bar window -- gives 0.819 / 0.780 / 0.696 / 0.585. Lift is +0.046 / +0.046 / +0.064 / +0.001. The whole apparent effect is that after a spike the reference is only ~1.0-1.2 xATR (2.0 ticks in ZB!) away, and after a grind it is 2.1-2.5 xATR (4-5 ticks) away. Nothing about the level or the failure causes the return.

RE-ENTRY AT THE ORIGINAL PRICE EARNS NOTHING ABOVE A GENERIC FAR LIMIT. When price abandons a 24-bar extreme close by >=1xATR and later comes back to touch it, a limit resting at that abandoned level is genuinely fillable. Fading the return (i.e. the abandoned high acts as resistance) gives ZB pooled +0.350 +/- 0.108 ticks at 12 bars (n=3922 fills, 1228 episodes, 343 days) and ZN +0.485 +/- 0.099 (n=5300 fills, 1647 episodes, 449 days). The matched control -- a limit at the SAME normalized distance with the SAME 48-bar TTL at random bars -- gives ZB +0.430 (sell side) / +0.245 (buy side) and ZN +0.494 / +0.412. The level contributes zero; the entire number is the generic 'a far limit that fills is followed by short-horizon reversion' effect. Outside ZB/ZN it is worse: ES pooled -1.141 +/- 0.894, YM -2.330 +/- 1.496, CL -0.516 +/- 0.469, 6E -0.031 +/- 0.181, ZF +0.385 +/- 0.135 against a control of +0.389/+0.225. Every one of them is under its own cost floor.

DEEPER LIMIT RE-ENTRY AFTER A FAILURE IS STRONGLY NEGATIVE, AND MOSTLY FOR A MECHANICAL REASON WORTH RECORDING. Resting a buy limit at (or just below) the notional stop price after a down-failure gives 12-bar drifts of -0.92, -0.97, -1.82, -4.49 ticks (ZB, speeds 1-2/3-5/6-11/12-23, ttl 24, n_filled 423/349/482/1191). Most of this is an ARTEFACT I want flagged: a limit at the stop price is already through the market at bar j, so it 'fills' at a price worse than available and the measurement is meaningless for shallow k. The only genuinely-resting variants (limit at stop - 1.0xATR, i.e. strictly below the failure bar's low) give +0.052 +/- 0.71 (ZB down-fail spike), -0.379 (ZB down-fail fast), -0.963 (mid), -3.013 (grind), +0.678 (ZB up-fail spike), -0.461 (up-fail fast), -0.786 (ZN up-fail mid), -2.418 (ZN up-fail grind). Chasing a failure deeper is not a thing; the grind numbers are just 'the drift kept drifting'.

FAILURE STATE DOES NOT IMPROVE LIQUIDITY-PROVISION ECONOMICS AT ALL -- this was the mission's stated highest-value target and it came back empty. Direction-neutral (buy-below + sell-above pooled), ZB+ZN pooled, ttl 6, hold 12 bars. Baseline over every 3rd tradable discovery bar: depth 1 +0.485 +/- 0.021 (n=92,503 fills, p_touch 0.839), depth 2 +0.559 +/- 0.027 (n=63,635, pt 0.576), depth 3 +0.556 +/- 0.037 (pt 0.377), depth 4 +0.514 +/- 0.050 (pt 0.249). At failure bars, depth 2: spike +0.563 +/- 0.147, fast +0.585 +/- 0.150, mid +0.631 +/- 0.127, grind +0.495 +/- 0.085. Every cell is within ~1 SE of baseline. edge_ratio is likewise flat (1.094-1.126 vs baseline 1.129). P(touch) barely moves (0.596 spike vs 0.576 baseline at depth 2). A failure event tells you nothing about whether the next limit fill will be a good one.

THE ZB/ZN LIQUIDITY-PROVISION BASELINE ITSELF DOES NOT CLEAR THE COST FLOOR. Unconditionally, a resting limit 2 ticks away with ttl 6 that gets filled earns +0.559 +/- 0.027 ticks over the next 12 bars (ZB+ZN pooled, direction-neutral, n=63,635 fills). ZB alone: buy-2-below +0.388, sell-2-above +0.558. The honest limit-entry cost floor is 0.794t (ZB) and 0.938t (ZN). So the generic market-making edge in the treasury complex is REAL (it is 20+ SE from zero and identical in both halves of discovery: 0.566 / 0.551) but UNTRADEABLE by a margin of ~0.3 ticks. Any candidate must beat +0.56, not zero.

SCALE REALITY CHECK THAT KILLS SEVERAL FRAMINGS: the median 5-minute ATR is 1.64 ticks in ZB and 1.86 in ZN. A '1xATR adverse excursion' in ZB is 2 ticks -- barely twice the cost floor. The failure events I was asked to construct are, in the treasuries, noise-scale events. This is why every ZB/ZN failure statistic here has an effect size measured in fractions of a tick. Other markets for reference: ZF 2.00, 6E 3.07, CL 8.93, ES 10.71, YM 16.79 ticks.

DAY OF WEEK IS NOTHING in ZB and ZN. With day-clustered standard errors, all 20 cells (5 weekdays x 2 horizons x 2 markets) have |t| <= 1.65. ZB Wednesday 48-bar drift -1.754 ticks looks large but its clustered SE is 1.234 (t=-1.42, 110 days). The naive per-bar SE for the same cell was 0.102, giving a spurious t of -6.0 — overlapping 48-bar windows inflated it 12x. Any day-of-week result computed without clustering in this project is wrong.

MINUTE OF HOUR IS NOTHING directionally. Across all 12 five-minute slots in both markets, forward 12-bar drift ranges from -0.068 to -0.002 ticks with SEs of 0.065-0.077 — no slot is distinguishable from any other. There IS a real range/volume signature: the :05 and :35 bars are 30% and 19% larger in range and 40%/28% larger in volume than the other ten slots (ZB :05 = 2.458 ticks vs :30 = 1.818), reflecting top-of-hour and half-hour prints. It carries no direction.

THE STRUCTURALLY LARGEST BARS OF THE DAY CARRY NO DIRECTIONAL EDGE. Testing the 13:35 UTC release bar, the 07:05 EU open bar, the 22:05 Globex reopen bar, the 20:00 US close bar and the 00:05 midnight bar, in both markets, both unrestricted and restricted to range>1.5x ATR, signed by the bar's own direction, at 4 horizons — 40 cells, one event per day so episodes = days = raw and the observations are genuinely independent. The largest |t| anywhere is 2.25 (ZN midnight bar, range>1.5xATR, 3-bar drift -0.558, n=147 days), which does not survive 40 comparisons. The reopen bar shows a consistent mild fade in both markets (ZB -0.591 at 24 bars t=-1.50; ZN -0.802 t=-1.21) but never reaches significance and never reaches the cost floor.

OVERNIGHT AND DAILY GAPS DO NOT FADE PROFITABLY. Reopen gap (22:00 UTC open vs last pre-halt close, mean |gap| 1.64t ZB / 1.81t ZN): fading it earns +0.414 ticks at 6 bars in ZB (t=2.34, 181 days) and +0.358 in ZN (t=2.10, 218 days), then decays to nothing by 12-24 bars. Both are below their 0.794 / 0.938 cost floors and are 2 cells out of ~12 tested. Restricting to |gap|>=2 ticks makes it worse and underpowered (ZB n=49). Daily gaps (first bar of day vs prior close, 333 ZB / 442 ZN days): fade drift t <= 1.69 at every horizon, nothing.

VOLATILITY-STATE TRANSITIONS ARE NOT TRADEABLE AS EVENTS. Four causal transition definitions (atr_pct .2->.7 over 24 bars, .8->.3, +0.3 rising, -0.3 falling) x 3 horizons x 2 markets. The only cell reaching z>3 against the bar-shuffle null is vol_hi->lo (atr_pct .8 -> .3): ZB 48-bar +2.758 ticks (day-clustered t=2.17) and ZN 48-bar +2.380 (t=3.02). It fails on power and stability: ZB has 54 de-overlapped episodes on 61 days, below the project's 60-episode floor; ZN has 82 episodes on 80 days but splits H1 +4.48 / H2 +1.41 at 48 bars, and the effect is an unconditional LONG bias in a two-year sample that contained large bond rallies after volatility spikes. Not a finding. The other three transition states have |z| < 2 everywhere.

'CALM VOLATILITY' ADDS NOTHING TO THE INCUMBENT IMPULSE FINDING. The incumbent record is '+0.47 ticks from a 2-tick buy limit after a 24-bar up-impulse >1.25x ATR in calm volatility'. I measured the identical statistic with no conditioning at all — every tradable ZB discovery bar, 70,580 of them — and got +0.474 ticks. The impulse and calm-vol conditions contribute zero. The stated P(touch) ladder (0.80 / 0.49 / 0.27 / 0.14 at depths 1-4) also matches the unconditional ladder I measured (0.825 / 0.564 / 0.370 / 0.245), and the rising edge_ratio with depth is reproduced by a zero-edge bar-shuffle of the same data.

LARGEST BAR OF THE DAY AND LARGEST VOLUME BAR OF THE DAY ARE NULL. Day's largest range bar occurring after bar 24 (ZB n=2,320 / 673 episodes; ZN n=2,627 / 844): 12-bar drift +0.028 (z=-0.09) and -0.124 (z=-1.41). Day's max-volume bar after bar 24 (ZB n=2,062 / 871 episodes; ZN n=2,554 / 1,137): 12-bar day-clustered t = -0.75 and -0.07. Bar range > 4x ATR is underpowered in both markets (n=143 / 169, raw below the 200 threshold) and gives opposite signs (ZB -0.042, ZN +0.598).

PASSIVE PROVISION FAILS IN ALL 12 MARKETS TESTED, NOT JUST ZB/ZN. Best-case (fill every touch) 12-bar value from a depth-2 limit versus the honest cost floor in ticks: ZB 0.474 vs 0.794; ZN 0.622 vs 0.938; ZF 0.463 vs 1.226; ES 0.298 vs 2.090; 6E 0.143 vs 1.930; 6B 0.243 vs 3.210; CL 0.076 vs 2.850; ZC 0.427 vs 0.970; and NEGATIVE even before costs in YM (-0.389), RTY (-0.284), GC (-0.289), HG (-0.085). ZB and ZN are indeed the least-bad, at 60% and 66% of their floors, but no market clears. This is the definitive breadth check on the liquidity-provision thesis.

TRAPPED TRADERS DO NOT EXIST IN 5-MIN OHLCV. Six trap constructions (close beyond prior-day high/low then back inside within 12 bars; intrabar sweep of prior-day high/low with close back inside; intrabar sweep of the running day extreme with close back inside) x 12 markets = 64 powered cells. Cells with |t|>2 on 12-bar drift: 0 of 64. Cells where the trap direction was even correct in sign: 36 of 64 — an exact coin flip (binomial p=0.51). The largest |t| in the entire family is HG T13_sweep_dayhi at t=-1.92 and HG T12_sweep_pdl at t=-1.89, both wrong-signed relative to the story. ZB T1_trapped_long: +0.059 ticks, t=+0.20, n_raw=3140, 273 episodes. Market-entry edge_ratio across all 64 trap cells clusters tightly on 1.00 (range 0.85-1.23), i.e. no excursion asymmetry either. The 'trapped longs must liquidate' story has no measurable footprint whatsoever.

FORCED ACTORS (SESSION OPENS, EOD FLATTEN, ROLL) ARE NULL. 120 powered cells across 12 markets covering the 13:30 UTC macro window, the 14:30 UTC equity open, the 19:12-20:12 UTC pre-EOD-flatten hour, the 22:00 UTC reopen, and quarterly roll windows. Cells with |t|>2 at 12 bars: 2 of 120 (and they are the same cell reported twice as long and short — GC pre-EOD, t=+/-2.18, which fails split-half and is gold's 2025 trend leaking into whichever bucket you look at). Roll windows specifically: 24 cells, maximum |t| = 1.24 — the quarterly roll leaves no measurable footprint in any of the 12 markets. Best equity-index cells (YM reopen t=1.88, RTY pre-EOD t=1.84) do not survive and disagree with each other in sign.

THE HONEST LIMIT SWEEP IS EMPTY. 584 through-fill cells (12 markets x 16 generic scale-free states x depths 1-4, pen=1, day-clustered SE, all with >=60 episodes). Positive drift: 68/584. Clears commission alone: 11/584. Clears the honest cost floor: 3/584. Clears floor AND t>2: 1/584. Clears floor AND t>2 AND both chronological halves same sign AND n_raw>=500: 0/584. The single survivor before the n_raw filter is NG weak_close_up_bar depth4: +4.287 ticks, t=2.26, but n_raw=278 with a 95% CI of [+0.51, +7.82] — right at the underpowered boundary and useless for sizing.

THE DIRECTIONAL SWEEP IS EMPTY. 816 powered directional cells (generic states + participant stories, all markets). Effect exceeds a market-entry cost of commission+1.0t slip+0.15t stop slip in 14 cells; effect exceeds that cost AND t>2 in 0 cells. 73 cells have |t|>2 but every one of them is far below its cost: the largest are ZB big_up_bar +0.343t (t=3.57) vs 1.294t cost, ZB fast_up_3bar +0.294t (t=3.47) vs 1.294t, ZN big_dn_bar +0.320t (t=3.24) vs 1.438t, ZN big_up_bar +0.321t (t=2.87) vs 1.438t. Every single one is a restatement of the same rates-reversion finding, and every single one misses cost by roughly 1 full tick.

GC AFTER A CALM UP-IMPULSE IS A REGIME, NOT A STRUCTURE. The only large-n cell that came close: GC impulse_up_calm (24-bar move >1.25 ATR, ATR percentile <0.5), buy limit 4 ticks below close, through-fills only. Drift +2.305 ticks, t=2.17, n_raw=18,426, 1,249 episodes, 448 days — genuinely well-powered. But the cost floor is 2.850 ticks, so it does not clear even at face value, and the chronological split-half is fatal: first half +0.212 ticks, second half +4.193 ticks, a 20x gap. This is gold's 2025 bull run, not a repeatable behaviour. The mirror state (GC impulse_dn_calm, sell) is -3.9 ticks (t=-3.3), i.e. the same trend showing up with the opposite sign — confirming trend contamination rather than structure.

RTY AND YM GAVE OPPOSITE SIGNS FOR AN IDENTICAL STATE, AND BOTH WERE NOISE. day_low_area (pos_in_day<0.15), buy: RTY +3.251 ticks, YM -3.145 ticks, on ~12,000 raw bars each. Two highly correlated US equity index futures cannot genuinely disagree by 6.4 ticks on the same state. Cause diagnosed: core.drift_profile bootstraps over RAW overlapping bars, so its CI is ~sqrt(raw/episodes) ≈ 3.7x too narrow. Re-measured with a day-clustered bootstrap, RTY day_low_area is t=1.13 and YM is t<1 — both indistinguishable from zero. This is a live methodology bug affecting any ranking built on drift_profile's CI, not just these two cells.

THE COST RANKING IN THE PROJECT BRIEF IS INVERTED ONCE THE ADVERSE BUFFER IS CHARGED. On commission alone ZB is indeed the cheapest market measured — 0.144 ticks = 8.4% of a 5-min ATR, matching the brief's ~7%. But the honest floor (commission + 0.15t expected stop slip + 0.5t adverse buffer) is a fixed number of TICKS, and ZB's 5-min ATR is only 1.71 ticks, so the buffer alone eats 29% of an ATR. Honest floor as a percentage of one 5-min ATR, best to worst: GC 17.8%, ES 19.6%, YM 25.6%, RTY 27.5%, NG 27.8%, HG 29.6%, CL 30.5%, ZB 46.3%, ZN 48.6%, ZF 57.2%, 6E 65.1%, ZT 109.4%. ZB and ZN rank 8th and 9th of 12, not 1st and 2nd. Worse, the same property that makes ZB cheap in commission (a large tick relative to bar range) is exactly what makes its limit fills queue-dependent: corr(log ATR-in-ticks, fraction-of-fills-that-are-exact-touches) = -0.992 across the 12 markets. Cheap-in-commission and safe-in-queue are structurally opposed, and ZB is at the wrong end of the trade-off.

ZT IS UNCONDITIONALLY COST-DEAD. Honest floor 0.938 ticks against a median 5-min ATR of 0.86 ticks — the cost of a round turn exceeds the entire average 5-minute range (109.4%). The median ZT 5-min bar has a range of exactly 1 tick and 80.4% of limit 'fills' are exact touches. No state can clear this; do not spend further compute on ZT. 6E is nearly as bad at 65.1% of ATR with a 47.9% exact-touch rate.

SEQUENCES / FORMATION ALPHABET (assignment a): 1,585 combinations tested = {ZB,ZN} x {long,short} x 3 bracket geometries x {9 single letters, 81 two-step words, up to 729 three-step words}, filtered to n_fill>=200. Largest |lift| was 1.48 ticks but on 107 episodes; the largest block-clustered |t| in the whole family was 4.20. For ~1,600 correlated tests the expected family maximum is 3.4-3.6, so nothing exceeded noise. No word replicated across both markets, both sides, or the three geometries.

PATH DEPENDENCE, formally tested (assignment a): for each end-letter, do the 9 possible predecessor letters produce different outcomes? 108 end-state tests (2 markets x 2 sides x 3 geometries x up to 9 end-letters) on the de-overlapped episode sample. A naive chi-square found 25.9% of tests at p<0.05 (vs 5% expected) with min p<0.0001 - but that excess is serial clustering, not predecessor information: a permutation test that shuffles the predecessor label WITHIN each end-state (preserving everything else) gave only ~8/108 at perm_p<0.05 against ~5 expected, min perm_p 0.000 in a single cell (ZN long, end=6, one geometry) that collapsed to 0.015 and 0.122 in the other two geometries. Bonferroni threshold 0.00046, nothing near it. VERDICT: path dependence at the single-bar formation-letter level does not exist in ZB/ZN at a magnitude this data can detect. Note the methodological trap for the project: the chi-square version of this test is badly anti-conservative on overlapping financial data and would have produced a confident false positive.

COARSE-STATE CHAINS (assignment a): state = (12-bar direction tercile) x (12-bar span tercile) = 9 states; 734 two-step and three-step chains with n_raw>=200. Best was ZB short 2>3>1 with lift +1.48t but only 107 episodes and t=4.40, in a family of 734 correlated tests. The two largest chains with real size (ZN short 2>3, 594 episodes, t=3.94; ZN short 3>2, 650 episodes, t=3.54) did not have counterparts in ZB or on the long side. No chain survived.

PAIRS AND TRIPLES SCAN (assignment b): 74 individually-weak binary conditions (quintile extremes of 32 causal features, plus session, day-of-week, vol regime, trend regime), all singles and pairs plus triples among the 30 strongest singles = 5,014 to 5,322 combinations per family, four families (ZB/ZN x long/short) = 20,479 combinations. Family-wise max-statistic null (circular whole-day shift of the outcome array, whole scan re-run, 12 shifts per family) gave null max|t| medians of 4.80 to 7.37 and maxima of 5.99 to 8.12 - i.e. in a family this size a |t| below about 6 is completely unremarkable. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the block-clustered t used in this scan was subsequently found to be biased (it compares a block-weighted state mean to a fill-weighted baseline mean, producing |t|>10 on combinations whose lift is +0.02 ticks). The t column and the FWER p-values from this scan are therefore DISCARDED. The lift column is valid, and the largest lift on any combination with real size was +0.38t (ZB short, ret24_hi+pos_in_day_hi, 4,303 fills) - half the cost floor. The one combination with a big lift (ZB long, bars_since_lo_lo+atr_pct_hi+dow3, +1.27t) has 361 fills across 61 blocks and includes a day-of-week term; it is a textbook triple-interaction overfit and was not pursued.

DIRECTION x QUOTE-SIDE INTERACTION (assignment b): the liquidity-provision prediction that a buy-limit-below filled on a pullback after an up-move should behave differently from a sell-limit-above filled on continuation is FALSE in this data. Extreme deciles of ret1, ret3 and ret12 hurt both quote sides roughly equally: e.g. ret1 top decile, 6 cells each, mean lift long -0.155 and short -0.026; ret1 bottom decile long -0.151 and short -0.129; ret3 top decile long -0.150 and short -0.102. No side asymmetry large enough to trade.

MOVE x VOLUME INTERACTION (assignment b): the classic 'big move on low volume reverts, big move on high volume continues' separation does not appear. ret1 extreme decile split by volume tercile: UPx_volHI long -0.239 / short -0.080, UPx_volLO long -0.168 / short -0.121, DNx_volHI long -0.218 / short -0.156, DNx_volLO long -0.178 / short -0.098. All four cells negative on both sides; volume does not separate them.

ALIGNED vs OPPOSED QUOTING (the strongest surviving interaction, still untradeable): resting the limit on the side the market has been moving toward (buy limit below after a 24-bar decline; sell limit above after a 24-bar advance) beats the opposite in 24 of 36 market x geometry x side cells, mean +0.098 ticks, and replicates in held-out validation (28/36 cells, mean +0.169t). In ZB/ZN specifically it is 9/12 cells, mean +0.075t. This is probably a real property of the market, but at +0.07 to +0.17 ticks it is 5-11x below the 0.794/0.938-tick cost floor. REAL BUT UNTRADEABLE.

POSITIVE-LIFT STATES, economically motivated hunt: three pre-entry conditions that should isolate uninformed flow were tested on ZB/ZN x 3 geometries x 2 sides. (a) 'quiet' (bottom tercile of volume AND bar range AND 6-bar span simultaneously): 10/12 cells positive in discovery, mean +0.144t, but mean block t of only +0.27 and validation 5/12 with mean -0.067t. Dead. (b) limit price still inside the trailing 12-bar range: 0/12 positive. (c) limit price at the edge of the 12-bar range (a fill would set a new extreme): 12/12 positive in discovery, mean +0.077t with enormous apparent t - but validation 8/12 with mean -0.014t. This one is a TRAP worth flagging: a fill at a new range extreme is a fill at the most bid-side print available, so it maximises the bar-touch bid-ask-bounce artifact described in finding 2; the discovery signal is measurement, not money, and it duly vanishes out of sample.

RARE EVENTS, states failing the power floor (assignment c, reported as UNDERPOWERED-BUT-INTERESTING and NOT as findings): ZN long, 6+ consecutive down closes - lift +2.08t, t=4.06, but n_raw=119 and 55 episodes. ZB short, 6+ consecutive up closes - lift +1.94t but n_raw=91 and 41 episodes. ZB long, bar range >4x ATR - lift -1.57t but n_raw=143. 12-bar squeeze (span12<0.35 ATR) - n_raw=197, 30-34 episodes. All below the 200-raw / 60-episode floor and none is reportable. The run-length states are the most interesting of these and are the only thing in this campaign I would spend more data on.

RARE EVENTS that DID pass the power floor and were still negative or non-replicating: at_pdl (price within 0.15 ATR of the prior day low) gave ZB short +0.58t (t=2.13) but ZN short -0.33t (t=-2.26) - opposite signs across the two treasuries, so noise. reopen_30m (22:00-22:30 UTC, p_touch only 0.396 because the book is thin) gave ZB short +0.52 to +0.68t at t~1.7-1.9, the single most interesting positive rare state, but it does not appear in ZN and did not survive as a candidate. eu_open_15m gave ZN short +0.27t (t=2.22) and nothing elsewhere. All the strongly significant rare states were NEGATIVE: first bars of the US session (ZN long -1.32t, t=-3.56), 13:30 UTC macro window (ZN long -0.88t, t=-3.10), bar range >3 ATR (ZB long -1.06t, t=-3.24), 1-bar move >2 ATR (ZN long -1.08t, t=-2.85), volume spike with a big move (both markets, ~-0.43t). These all point at the same thing as finding 1 and were folded into it.

NULL RESULT ON THE MISSION'S CENTRAL QUESTION: no state was found in which limit fills are followed by favourable excursion asymmetry LARGE ENOUGH TO TRADE. Across roughly 23,000 tested state/combination/chain cells in ZB and ZN, the largest lift over the unconditional baseline that also (i) had >=200 raw and >=60 episodes, (ii) replicated in both halves of discovery, (iii) replicated in held-out validation, and (iv) held sign in both markets, was the ALIGNED-quoting effect at +0.075 to +0.098 ticks - about one tenth of the cost floor. The only robust, replicating, economically coherent effect at or above the cost floor is NEGATIVE (finding 1). The organic answer to 'what does this market repeatedly do that a liquidity provider can be paid for' is, on this data, 'nothing that OHLCV can see'.
